sources.letters_2021: Privy Council Office, Letters on the Implementation of the Call to Action on Anti-Racism, Equity, and Inclusion in the Federal Public Service (90 letters, 2021). https://www.canada.ca/en/privy-council/corporate/clerk/call-to-action-anti-racism-equity-inclusion-federal-public-service/letters-implementation.html

sources.representation: Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat, Employment equity public service representation by department or agency with departmental workforce availability estimates (2021 and 2025 tables).

method: Commitments, goals, progress and barriers are short summaries of each published document, not the full text. Read the linked original for the complete letter or self-assessment. Goal status is read from the summary: set, work under way, or no goal stated. A goal stated in a document is not evidence that it was met.
method_fr: Les engagements, objectifs, progrès et obstacles sont de brefs résumés de chaque document publié, et non le texte intégral. Consultez l’original pour la lettre ou l’autoévaluation complète. L’état de chaque objectif est tiré du résumé : fixé, travaux en cours ou aucun objectif indiqué. Un objectif inscrit dans un document ne prouve pas qu’il a été atteint.

letter.author: Philip Rizcallah, Chief Executive Officer
commitments: Set hiring goals that exceed labour market availability and use targeted outreach to people with disabilities and other equity-seeking groups.
Make job posters, communications, tools and the external website accessible, and provide individual accommodations and flexible work hours.
Recruit diverse members, including Indigenous and Black candidates, to the technical committees developing accessibility standards.
Engage Indigenous organizations on technical committee roles, research funding and priorities (Indigenous research proposals rose from 2% to 21% of funds received).
Create a charter formalizing the commitment to anti-racism, equity and inclusion, name a diversity and inclusion champion, and require unconscious bias training for all staff.
Develop a multi-year staffing plan that integrates talent management with succession planning.

letter.author: Orlando Da Silva, LSM, Chief Administrator
commitments: Endorsed the 2021-22 diversity workplan and will develop a principle-based multi-year action plan.
Created a Diversity Network (December 2020) as a consultative body.

Use name-blind screening and assessments, treat employment equity gaps as justification for selection, and recruit Indigenous and visible minority applicants from the Federal Student Work Experience Program.
Delivered a Group Language Training Program (2020) that trained 120 employees in one year.
Make unconscious bias training mandatory for managers with staffing delegation and extend it to managers without delegation and others involved in hiring.
Make the Diversity Accreditation Program mandatory and use representative selection boards for collective staffing processes.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goal set for Indigenous peoples: goal to managers to eliminate all representation gaps (Indigenous gap -5; visible minorities +29).

inclusion.text: Goals set in the EDI Strategy and 2022-2025 Action Plan; 2023 PSES inclusion results better than the public service as a whole, but almost half of Black/racialized employees say not enough is done on anti-racism and would not feel comfortable speaking up if victims of racism.

progress: EDI Strategy and 2022-2025 Action Plan in place, with progress reports every six months.
Inclusive hiring training for all hiring managers, mandatory for staffing sub-delegation holders, plus an intranet guide.
EX/LC performance agreements include an EDI measure; staff complete at least 6 hours of D&I training per year and managers at least 9 hours.
Talent Management Program: 8 of 9 in the last cohort were from at least one employment equity group; Mentorship Plus to launch in fall 2024.
barriers: Data quality and availability: the former HR system could not provide mobility demographics by equity group.
Small organization with limited resources; the same few people carry many priorities.
No disaggregated Black/racialized data, pending the TBS updated self-identification questionnaire.

letter.author: Chris Forbes, Deputy Minister
commitments: Launched targeted recruitment for Indigenous, Black and other racialized candidates and persons with disabilities in under-represented job categories (students, administrative professionals, research technicians, executives).
Continued the Indigenous Student Recruitment Initiative, which hired 44 students in the previous year.
Launch a sponsorship program in fall 2021 to prepare high-potential employees from equity-seeking groups for leadership roles.
Undertake an employment systems review to ensure HR policies and services are free of bias.
Develop a diversity and inclusion index based on Public Service Employee Survey results and workforce data, to launch in fall 2021.
Established the Indigenous Pathfinder Service to help Indigenous peoples access federal agriculture programs.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Short-term recruitment goals for all designated employment equity groups, set by occupational group in the 2022-25 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan and reviewed annually; branch employment equity plans set staffing and recruitment targets to close gaps by 2025, based on workforce availability.

black_recruitment.text: Same short-term recruitment goals framework as for all designated employment equity groups (2022-25 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan).

racialized_recruitment.text: Same short-term recruitment goals framework as for all designated employment equity groups (2022-25 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan).

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals in the 2022-25 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan, with a Monitoring Framework of activities, performance objectives, indicators, baselines and targets; each branch has an employment equity plan with targets to close representation gaps by 2025; each Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Network sets its own annual inclusion goals.

progress: Expanded the Diverse Staffing Board Initiative in 2022 (73 registered volunteers; supported 12 of 15 staffing processes in 2023-24).
720 employees completed Inclusive Hiring Practices training by March 2024, with 100% compliance among managers with staffing sub-delegation.
Ran targeted processes and department-wide talent inventories for employment equity group members, plus an executive recruitment plan for racialized candidates.
Publishes an annual diversity, equity and inclusion report card and monitors the Strategy bi-annually against its Monitoring Framework.
barriers: Reluctance to self-identify and the voluntary, changeable nature of self-identification make metrics and trend measurement unreliable.

Self-identification data cannot be used for anything but statistical reporting without the person's consent; a Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Consent Form (December 2022) was created to allow its use for nominations to development initiatives.
Promotion goals for employment equity groups are not yet set; they are to be added in the 2026-2029 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Action Plan.

organizations.notes: No numeric representation targets stated in the letter; promotion goals not yet set in the self-assessment.

letter.author: Francis P. McGuire
commitments: Implement the two-year Employment Equity, Inclusion and Anti-Racism Action Plan (six pillars); over 60% of planned deliverables completed.
Created the Office of Inclusion, Equity and Anti-Racism in October 2020 to lead and coordinate the work.
Delivered the Diversity. Inclusion. Competence. Excellence. (DICE) learning series; all executives completed it by March 31, 2021 and 66% of employees had participated.
Created an EX-1 leadership development position tailored to Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees and persons with disabilities.
Added an employment equity, diversity and inclusion indicator to all executive performance management agreements, with a Truth and Reconciliation indicator to be added.
Joined the Building Black Leaders program and led the Selection Board+ initiative to diversify staffing selection boards.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Overall representation 13% above workforce availability (WFA) in 2023-24 (met), 19% above in 2024-25, 25% above in 2025-26, for Indigenous peoples, racialized people including Black employees, and persons with disabilities.

racialized_recruitment.text: Overall representation 13% above WFA in 2023-24 (met), 19% above in 2024-25, 25% above in 2025-26, for Indigenous peoples, racialized people including Black employees, and persons with disabilities.

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotions of Indigenous employees at or above their representation (4.5% of employees); 9.3% of promotions in 2023-24 were Indigenous employees (objective exceeded).

racialized_promotion.text: Promotions of racialized employees at or above their representation (9.2% of employees, 3.1% Black); 9.3% of promotions in 2023-24 were racialized employees and 3.1% Black (objective met).

inclusion.text: Support existing employee-led networks and create new ones for equity-seeking groups; DICE conversation mandatory for all employees (over 85% participated); Valuing Diversity and Inclusion competency mandatory on management posters since January 2023.

progress: Met the year-one objective of 13% above WFA and was meeting the year-two objective of 19% above WFA.
80% of completed staffing processes from September 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024 were intentional hiring processes.
Created new employee-led networks in 2023 for Black employees, Multicultural employees, Indigenous employees, Employees with disabilities, and Women and Allies.
Vice-presidents must sponsor two Indigenous, Black/racialized, persons with disabilities or 2SLGBTQIA+ employees; lack of progress can affect performance pay.
barriers: The forward direction excluded women, persons with disabilities and 2SLGBTQIA+ people, which did not align with the Agency's existing EEIAR Action Plan and staffing objectives.
As a small department, balancing robust intentional recruitment objectives with support for internal talent development was challenging.
Workforce availability benchmarking relies on outdated Treasury Board Secretariat data at national level only, which does not reflect Atlantic Canada or National Capital Region availability.

organizations.notes: No separate Black recruitment or promotion goals; Black employees are included in the racialized goals.

letter.author: John Ossowski
commitments: Created Anti-Racism Task Force in March 2021 to draft and implement an anti-racism strategy; Anti-Racism Unit to carry it out over three years with regular reporting to the senior executive table.

Launched EE Executive Leadership Development Program, Building Black Leaders Initiative, a second mentorship program for visible minorities, and targeted EE EX-01/EX-02 staffing processes (650 applications received).

Made anti-racism/unconscious bias training mandatory for executives (92% of executives took unconscious bias training; 87% of senior executives took anti-racism statement workshops; 706 middle managers trained in character-based leadership).
Developing all-employee anti-racism training with union partners, informed by an employee survey on root causes of racism.
Developed 2021-2024 EE, Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan and a Culture Performance Measurement Framework to track culture change and reasons for leaving.
Expanded Employee Assistance Program support for employees affected by racism and refined Informal Conflict Management approach to address racism.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Set recruitment goals for Indigenous peoples, using workforce availability data; goals communicated via Agency-wide messages and developed with EE networks and advisory circles.

racialized_recruitment.text: Set recruitment goals for racialized people, using workforce availability data.

inclusion.text: Goals to foster greater inclusion in the Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan and Accessibility Plan, measured via PSES belonging, accommodation, discrimination and harassment indicators; 2024-2027 action plan sets goals to reduce gaps between equity-deserving communities and counterparts.

progress: Closed employment equity gaps for all categories except persons with disabilities (per TBS report); Reconciliation and Anti-Racism/EDI are 2 of 7 Agency priorities.
EE Executive Leadership Development Pilot (2022-23) had 11 graduates from equity-deserving groups; 4 appointed indeterminately or acting by March 31, 2024.
Executives mentored 21 Indigenous and 229 racialized employees and sponsored 17 Indigenous and 143 racialized employees over three years.
Ran 128 Indigenous-focused outreach events in 2023-24 and employs two Indigenous Career Navigators; 32.1% of language training participants in 2023-24 were racialized (vs 10.1% in 2022-23).
barriers: Self-identification rate about 60% vs goal of 80%; employees cite stigma, career impact and confidentiality concerns, especially frontline staff disclosing disabilities.
Outdated self-identification process/vocabulary; data integrity issues from timeliness of personnel information.
Official language requirements remain a significant barrier to career mobility, notably for Indigenous peoples, racialized employees and persons with disabilities.

letter.author: Manon Brassard
commitments: Build diversity and inclusion commitments into executive performance agreements.
Require hiring managers to provide a rationale when qualified equity-group candidates are not selected.
Run a self-identification campaign to destigmatize self-identification and get an accurate picture of the workforce.
Create a working group of employees with disabilities to develop a three-year action plan to remove barriers they experience.
Establish a mental health ombud service and safe spaces with concrete tools for employees affected by racism and discrimination.
Implement inclusive hiring practices linked to the 2019-2022 Integrated Human Resources Plan.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Three-year recruitment and promotion goals (indeterminate appointments) specific to certain occupational groups, set after analysis showed under-representation of Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees at all levels and regions; goals also set for persons with disabilities.

black_recruitment.text: Three-year recruitment and promotion goals (indeterminate appointments) specific to certain occupational groups, set after analysis showed under-representation of Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees at all levels and regions.

racialized_recruitment.text: Three-year recruitment and promotion goals (indeterminate appointments) specific to certain occupational groups, set after analysis showed under-representation of Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees at all levels and regions.

indigenous_promotion.text: Three-year promotion goals (indeterminate appointments) specific to certain occupational groups, as part of the same goals as recruitment.

black_promotion.text: Three-year promotion goals (indeterminate appointments) specific to certain occupational groups, as part of the same goals as recruitment.

racialized_promotion.text: Three-year promotion goals (indeterminate appointments) specific to certain occupational groups, as part of the same goals as recruitment.

inclusion.text: Maintain a turnover rate for Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees at least equal to or lower than the rate for employees as a whole; better define inclusion using Public Service Employee Survey results, the Employee Exit Questionnaire and employee consultations planned for summer/fall 2024.

progress: Set three-year recruitment and promotion goals for Indigenous, Black and racialized employees (plus persons with disabilities) and communicated them to all employees by memo from the Deputy Minister/President and at a Live at CED session.
President personally endorsed a winter 2024 recruitment campaign for Indigenous, Black and racialized students (Indigenous Student Employment Opportunity and Federal Student Work Experience Program).
Put quantitative and qualitative anti-racism and EDI goals in all executives' performance agreements; the 2024-25 common organizational goal for all staff is inclusion and accessibility.
Created a new EDI governance structure, a departmental EDI committee and a first EDI Forum; introduced a directive prioritizing second-language training for equity-seeking groups.
barriers: Small organization (400 employees) and small EDI team with limited resources, yet bound by the same commitments and obligations as larger organizations.
Difficulty consulting employees from employment equity groups: until recently there was only one employee network.

letter.author: Gitane De Silva, Chief Executive Officer
commitments: Established the Diversity and Belonging Team in April 2021, reporting to the CEO, to deliver an organization-wide Diversity and Belonging Roadmap (expected late fall 2021).
Created a Project Task Force on Gender Discrimination and issued an all-company letter clarifying conduct expectations in the field.

Formed the Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation Business Unit (December 2020), an Indigenous Advisory Committee to the Board and an Indigenous Employee Circle, and worked to finalize an Indigenous Employee Recruitment, Retention and Advancement Strategy.
Targeted student recruitment of racialized, religious-minority and Indigenous students, with mentoring and coaching, and launched a hiring program for Indigenous Monitors.
Made physical workplace changes including a smudge room, optical access buttons on washrooms and reception doors, and a gender-neutral fully accessible washroom and change room.
Launched a six-month hybrid-work pilot in October 2021 informed by a Gender Based Analysis+ assessment.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Indigenous peoples for 2023-24 and future years, using WEIMS/Employment Equity data to identify gaps, particularly at executive and professional levels.

black_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Black people for 2023-24 and future years, using WEIMS/Employment Equity data to identify gaps.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for racialized people for 2023-24 and future years, using WEIMS/Employment Equity data to identify gaps.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals set, guided by the Diversity and Belonging Roadmap, Employment Equity Plan and Indigenous Recruitment, Retention and Advancement Strategy, using Public Service Employee Survey, pulse survey, culture assessment and employment equity data.

progress: Reduced the representation gap for visible minorities and people with disabilities by 60% in one year (from a gap of 90 employees in 2021-22 to 35 in 2022-23); closed the visible minority gap in 2023-24 and narrowed the disability gap to six employees.
Indigenous representation reached 4.2%, above 2.6% labour market availability, and visible minorities reached 23.8%, above 23.5% labour market availability.
Appointed or hired four employees who self-identified as Indigenous, Black or racialized into indeterminate leadership roles (Director, Vice-President or Executive Vice-President).

Quantitative representation goals and an Inclusive Leadership accountability are in leaders' performance agreements, and progress on representation and inclusion goals is a criterion in talent management.

First year of the forward direction: increased representation through the Self-ID campaign and targeted student programs, stronger leadership engagement (training on labour relations, psychological safety and managing bias in hiring), greater transparency in reporting complaints and career development workshops, and a focus on psychological safety; mobility, retention and harassment/discrimination remain areas to improve.
barriers: Resistance to change and reluctance of some employees to self-identify as members of equity-deserving groups.
Resource constraints in securing enough funding, staffing and time to sustain the work long-term.
Ensuring accurate self-identification data and aligning goals with external labour market availability.

organizations.notes: The 2023-24 Employment Equity Report showed Indigenous representation at 4.2% (labour market availability 2.6%) and visible minorities at 23.8% (23.5%); the disability gap narrowed to six employees.

letter.author: Bob Hamilton, Commissioner of Revenue and Chief Executive Officer
commitments: Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan (EEDIAP) 2021-22 to 2024-25.
Leadership Learning Initiative (April 2021) with 50% of seats reserved for Indigenous peoples, visible minorities, and persons with disabilities.
Minimum two employment equity group members on all staffing boards for management and executive positions.
Indigenous Mentoring Initiative (13 pairings) and promotion of MentorMe to racialized employees.
Unconscious bias workshop mandatory for staffing board members; published an Ally Guide and Diversity and Inclusion Lens Handbook.
Two-year exhaustive review of staffing processes, a third-party employment systems review, and D&I performance measures embedded in executive performance agreements.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals based on labour market availability versus CRA demographics; aim for representation at or above LMA for all equity groups.

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals based on labour market availability versus CRA demographics; aim for representation at or above LMA for all equity groups.

inclusion.text: Strategic objectives and action plans for specific equity groups; unconscious bias training mandated (97% completed in 2023-24); Inclusion+ self-guided learning platform; developing a Directive on EDI.

progress: National Employment Equity Staffing Strategy: employment equity is the first staffing requirement in advertised non-EX processes where a gap exists; dynamic PowerBI EE Dashboard.
External Employment Systems Review completed, including a 2SLGBTQIA+ review; SponsorMe+ with 24 completed and 82 active participants.
Black Employee Network established June 2023; national executive staffing process for Indigenous peoples launched October 30, 2023, concluded February 2024, creating a pre-qualified pool.
Agency Leadership Development Program surpassed 70% participation from equity-deserving groups in 2022-23.
barriers: Access to disaggregated data: visible minority representation is above LMA overall but it is unclear whether Black employees are well represented, pending the TBS modernized Workforce Profile Questionnaire.
Lack of funding and resources for EDI work, especially networks.
Intersectionality adds complexity to the work.

letter.author: Taki Sarantakis, President
commitments: Require all employees and managers to complete 7 hours of dedicated learning (cultural bias, unconscious bias, harassment prevention, disability inclusion).
Implement the Employment Equity Action Plan 2021-2024 (12 concrete actions) based on the 32 recommendations of the early-2021 Employment Systems Review.
Create a Departmental Staffing Plan 2021-2022 focused on recruitment and promotion of under-represented employment equity groups, with branch-specific targets.
Chair the Mentorship Plus Interdepartmental Working Group for Small Departments and Agencies (31 organizations) and build a centralized mentor and sponsor database.
Led a joint recruitment initiative with nine other organizations, creating an inventory of nearly 2,000 employment equity candidates; more than 30 hired to date.
President personally mentors three executives through the Federal Black Employee Caucus.
targets: FY 2021-22 recruitment targets: 16 Indigenous recruits and 24 visible minority recruits (40 total).

indigenous_recruitment.text: Employment Equity Staffing Plan sets recruitment objectives overall and by branch and classification, based on demographics and 2016 Census workforce availability data.

racialized_recruitment.text: Same Employment Equity Staffing Plan objectives as for Indigenous employees.

indigenous_promotion.text: Employment Equity Staffing Plan sets promotion objectives for Indigenous employees.

racialized_promotion.text: Employment Equity Staffing Plan sets promotion objectives for racialized employees.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals for 2023-24 and beyond covering workforce diversity, inclusive culture, employee feedback (Public Service Employee Survey working group and action plan), mental health (13 psychosocial factors plus a 14th, anti-racism and equity, diversity and inclusion), and sponsorship and mentorship (Mentorship+ objective of one pairing per 100 employees).

progress: Mentorship+ Program exceeds its objective of one pairing per 100 employees (9 ongoing relationships for 700 employees).
President has sponsored several racialized, Black and Indigenous employees for development and promotion; nearly all executives registered as Mentorship+ sponsors or mentors.
Prioritizes official language training for Indigenous, Black and racialized employees ready for advancement.
Diversity and Employment Equity Action Plan 2021-2024 tracks key performance indicators including appointments and promotions of designated group members, with semi-annual data reviews.
barriers: Cannot set goals for Black employees without disaggregated Black workforce data; awaiting the new Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat self-identification form (goals to be explored in 2024-25).
Does not offer Indigenous language training and has no plans to do so.

organizations.notes: Black recruitment and promotion goals not set in the self-assessment.

commitments: Develop an inclusion and diversity framework with recruitment strategies focused on social, racial, gender and cultural diversity, including an intentional approach to job postings.
Conducted leadership and organizational diversity and inclusion training at the executive level.
Conduct an employment systems review in the coming year to identify major gaps in representation and form an employment equity, inclusion and anti-racism action plan.
Use employee surveys to provide leadership with information to guide Call to Action activities.

letter.author: Rita Notarandrea, Chief Executive Officer
commitments: Cultural awareness training for board, senior leadership and all staff via First People's Group, plus an Indigenous Gatherings series (first held National Indigenous Peoples Day 2021).
Unconscious bias training for all staff and OCAP (ownership, control, access and possession) training for most staff.
Editors now use Elements of Indigenous Style as a reference for their work.
Board statement 'Indigenous People and Communities: Health and Well-Being' committing to action on anti-racism and reconciliation.

Invited Assembly of First Nations, Thunderbird Partnership Foundation, Metis National Council and Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami to partner on Issues of Substance 2021, with culturally safe supports including an Indigenous support room.
Established Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Committee reporting to the CEO; updated Project Charter template to include EDI, anti-racism and decolonization; developing an EDI Policy Statement.
Voluntary self-identification questionnaire to benchmark workforce diversity and inform forward-looking action plans.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Work is underway to set goals; intended approach is to suggest hiring managers pull CVs from Public Service Commission fully or partially qualified pools that include Indigenous candidates and candidates with disabilities.

inclusion.text: CEO signed an inclusion pledge at a May 30, 2024 town hall committing to action on systemic discrimination and harassment, including microaggressions; Accessibility Plan implemented with progress reports; Accessibility Passport being implemented.

progress: CEO read and signed an inclusion pledge in front of all staff at a May 30, 2024 town hall; the pledge was posted on the intranet.
Implemented an Accessibility Plan with progress reports and is implementing the Accessibility Passport.
Human Resources developed an action plan to track activities and measure progress, updated regularly.
Created two gender-neutral washrooms and highlights commemorative days (Pride Month, religious celebrations, National Day for Truth and Reconciliation) on the intranet.
barriers: Micro-organization (85 employees) with no dedicated team for Call to Action initiatives; limited capacity to implement activities.
No mentorship program, no sponsorship of at least two Indigenous, Black or racialized employees, and no endorsed recruitment campaign yet.

letter.author: Siddika Mithani, Ph.D., President
commitments: Make unconscious bias training mandatory for all executives and work toward mandatory training for all employees.
Create a dedicated Anti-racism Task Force, starting with listening sessions for BIPOC employees in summer 2021.
Launch an updated Staffing Program in September 2021 reviewed through GBA+ and diversity and inclusion, with amended staffing values reflecting the Call to Action.
Commission a third-party Employment Systems Review in summer/fall 2021 to identify and eliminate barriers in hiring.

Support Indigenous employees through the Indigenous Summer Student Program (fifth year), a memorandum of understanding with the University of Guelph, and leadership programs (Indigenous Career Management for Employees and Indigenous Management Development Program).

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Indigenous peoples, using workforce availability gaps identified in quarterly and annual employment equity reporting as hiring targets.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for racialized people, using workforce availability gaps identified in quarterly and annual employment equity reporting as hiring targets.

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goals set for Indigenous employees, using workforce availability gaps as targets.

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals set for racialized employees, using workforce availability gaps as targets.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals set under the Diversity and Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan 2022-2025 and an Anti-Racism Action Plan, using Public Service Employee Survey data, self-identification data and the self-identification modernization project.

progress: Created an Anti-Racism Task Force and Anti-Racism Action Plan after six facilitated anti-racism discussion sessions in October 2021.
Created a BIPOC Career Navigator position and e-Binder, piloted in the west in summer 2023 and expanded agency-wide in May 2024.
Launched a BIPOC Official Language training program in November 2023, with over 115 candidates accepted.
Created an Indigenous Science Office staffed primarily by self-identified Indigenous employees and Indigenous Liaison Officer positions in each operations region.

Launched a national Diverse Selection Board Members Inventory in April 2023 (volunteers from equity-deserving groups supporting fair selection) and endorsed recruitment campaigns for Indigenous, Black and racialized employees, including a Project Management Development Program with spaces for BIPOC employees.

Anti-racism, equity and inclusion work embedded in the organizational plan and branch plans, with Integrated Business Planning rolling out to all branches in 2024-25; a Diversity Calendar and draft manager guidance on scheduling around religious and cultural observances.

First year of the forward direction: a cultural shift from empty words to tangible action, greater emphasis on accountability and transparency, and active employee engagement and collaboration, though change is slower than anticipated and fear of reprisal and audience fatigue remain concerns.
barriers: Data gaps and systemic bias: disaggregated data on Black employees is unavailable, so hiring, retention and promotion for this community cannot be measured and targeted recruitment is hard; immigrants with advanced degrees often occupy lower-level positions; limited personnel, budget and training resources.

Awareness and communication challenges: many employees are unaware of diversity and inclusion initiatives (audience fatigue from the volume of information), and EDI work is done 'off the side of their desks' alongside demanding primary jobs.

Perceptions of bias: extended acting appointments causing career stagnation for BIPOC employees, a 'prove it' attitude from management on experiences of race, tokenism and imposter syndrome, fear of reprisal for speaking up, and a sense that a neutral policy is not truly neutral.
Privacy concerns limit sharing and dissemination of sensitive employment equity data at a detailed level.
No agency-wide capacity to measure whether executive performance measures on the Call to Action have been met.

organizations.notes: Black recruitment and promotion goals not set: no disaggregated Black data. The agency does not offer Indigenous language training but directs individuals to Government of Canada Indigenous language resources.

letter.author: Doug Chorney, Chief Commissioner and Deputy Head (co-signed by the Executive Management Committee and Elizabeth Tabert, Chair, National EEDI Committee)
commitments: Multi-year employment equity, diversity, and inclusion plan guiding actions.
Use employment equity recruitment options and flexibilities and examine staffing methodology for systemic barriers.
Expand outreach and partnerships to promote the CGC as an accessible employer of choice.
Further education on unconscious bias, a speaker series, and evidence-based measures to monitor progress.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Work underway to set goals; goals to strengthen Indigenous recruitment rates.

racialized_recruitment.text: Work underway to set goals; goal to improve representation of all EE groups in Grain Inspector positions.

inclusion.text: Goals set; managers expected to contribute to equitable and transparent opportunities; each division has an action plan responding to 2022 PSES areas of concern.

progress: Closed the employment gap for racialized employees in Grain Inspector positions; Indigenous long-term acting appointments exceeded the expected rate; persons with disabilities indicators improved.
Workforce analysis report to the Executive Management Committee twice a year and a quarterly newsletter to all employees.
Common D&I work objective in all employees' 2023-24 performance agreements, with consequences for lack of progress; NEEDIC committee with executive co-champions.
Indigenous Career Navigator Program launched; Quarterly Diversity Speaker Series and shared Outlook calendar of commemorative dates (2023-24).
barriers: Small organization (under 500 employees) with limited resources and competing priorities; very small number of executive positions limits promotion-preparation programs.
Low turnover limits recruitment and promotion options.
Lack of recent data (workforce availability from the 2016 Census and 2017 Canadian Survey on Disability; no data on availability of racialized and Black workers).

letter.author: Isabelle Mondou, Deputy Minister, Canadian Heritage; Gina Wilson, Deputy Minister, Diversity and Inclusion and Youth, and Senior Associate Deputy Minister of Canadian Heritage
commitments: Three priority commitments (March 2021): promotion, sponsorship and career development of Indigenous, Black and other racialized groups and persons with disabilities; their recruitment and retention; and a review of all internal systems, policies, programs and initiatives.

Developed a three-year Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EEDI) strategy informed by employees with lived experience of racism and ableism, with concrete commitments and accountability, posted on the intranet with regular progress reporting.
Established the PCH Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) Review to examine programs for equitable access, engaging experts and applying lived-experience lenses to program design and delivery.
The Committee of Racialized Communities compiled a Book on Systemic Racism from employees' lived experiences, with recommendations for action.
Created two new governance committees co-chaired by the deputy ministers: Reconciliation and Indigenous Relations, and Diversity and Inclusion Oversight.
Supported expansion of the Black Employee Network from regional to national level and continued support for diverse employee networks.

Staffing: recruited or appointed six new executives from at least one employment equity group; launched an inventory of qualified Indigenous candidates in the National Capital Region; targeted external recruitment for Indigenous people (PM-05/PM-06) in one region; welcomed 12 Indigenous employees in the last year.

Learning: Reconciliation Strategic Framework and Reconciliation@PCH portal (May 2021); executives committed to learning on combatting racism and Indigenous realities; Deep Diversity Leadership training attended by nearly half of executives.

The Federal Anti-Racism Secretariat (housed at PCH) co-chaired the Learning Advisory Committee on Systemic Racism with the Canada School of Public Service, producing a Guide to Leading Conversations on Systemic Racism; the Knowledge Circle for Indigenous Inclusion launched a Career Roadmap, an Indigenous Ambassadors and Speakers Circle, and Wellness Talking and Sharing Circles.

Developing a new Talent Management and Professional Development Framework, consulted with employee-led committees (employment equity, (dis)ability, racialized communities, Indigenous working group, LGBTQ2+).

indigenous_recruitment.text: Multi-year recruitment targets set for Indigenous employees, based on Canadian population representation (workforce availability targets already met); specific goals in all executive performance agreements.

black_recruitment.text: Multi-year recruitment targets set for Black employees, based on Canadian population representation.

racialized_recruitment.text: Multi-year recruitment targets set for racialized employees, set at 25% above workforce availability to close the gap between 2016 census data and awaited 2021 census data.

indigenous_promotion.text: Multi-year promotion targets set for Indigenous employees (same basis as recruitment).

black_promotion.text: Multi-year promotion targets set for Black employees.

racialized_promotion.text: Multi-year promotion targets set for racialized employees.

inclusion.text: Work is underway to set inclusion goals; developing a Culture Statement and an IDEA Action Plan aiming for concrete, measurable, evidence-based qualitative and quantitative inclusion goals, using PSES and the internal 'Over to You' survey; the Accessibility Plan has 131 concrete actions.

progress: Set multi-year recruitment and promotion targets for Indigenous, Black and racialized employees using Canadian population data and sector, job-group and level segmentation; sector scorecards track progress and are shared on the intranet and with equity-deserving groups.

Every executive is asked to sponsor at least one Indigenous, Black, other racialized employee or person with a disability; nine employees selected for Mentorship Plus and two Mosaic Leadership Development Program participants completed the program and were promoted to EX-01.
The Deputy Head launched a recruitment campaign for racialized employees for EX-01 and EX-02 positions, increasing racialized employees in leadership.

Prioritized official language training for Indigenous, Black and racialized employees through a central fund and early access in performance agreements; language buddy program and coffee chats (about 34% of participants racialized, 19% Black).

Permanent Inclusion, Diversity, Equity and Accessibility (IDEA) Office (director, 7 FTEs, 2 temporary positions) reporting to a direct report of the Deputy Minister; each of seven employment equity and diversity networks receives $10,000 a year and 10 hours a month of work time.
Anti-racism, equity and inclusion work embedded in the organizational plan and branch plans; developing a calendar of significant religious, spiritual and cultural periods.
barriers: Establishing quantitative and qualitative baselines requires examining systemic issues previous generations of public service data do not capture; limited financial and technological resources impede comprehensive data collection and analysis.
Consultation fatigue: volunteer networks generously share lived experience, but balancing 'nothing about us, without us' with the burden engagement places on employees is a challenge.
Compounding barriers from multiple identities require further exploration, including ethical ways for employees to share lived experience while protecting privacy and well-being.

organizations.notes: Letter data annex: 2020-21 hires 416 (23 Indigenous, 78 racialized, 24 persons with disabilities); departures 226; executive hires 15, with equity-group figures suppressed (fewer than 5). The self-assessment notes the department does not currently offer Indigenous language training and has no plans to.

letter.author: Marie-Claude Landry, Chief Commissioner
commitments: Published the Anti-Racism Action Plan (first edition January 2021; second edition due September 2021) and bi-annual public progress reports.
Appointed a Racialized senior executive to champion sustainable anti-racist organizational change, attending weekly senior management meetings.
Launched a horizontal audit on the representation of Racialized people in executive and management positions in the federal public service (July 2020).
Increased the ratio of advertised staffing processes versus non-advertised appointments and ensured diversity on hiring boards.
Embedded anti-racism, equity and inclusion commitments in Executive Performance Accords and employee work objectives.

Conducted an independent third-party employment equity audit and an employment systems review, to be followed by an employment equity plan developed with unions and the Decolonization and Anti-Racism Consultation Committee.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Indigenous employees as part of a multifaceted recruitment strategy; aim to exceed Employment Equity Act representation targets (no numeric targets stated).

black_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Black employees as part of a multifaceted recruitment strategy; aim to exceed Employment Equity Act representation targets (no numeric targets stated).

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for racialized employees as part of a multifaceted recruitment strategy; aim to exceed Employment Equity Act representation targets (no numeric targets stated).

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goals set for Indigenous employees; includes leveraging non-advertised and acting appointments and a Mentorship Plus program in final development.

black_promotion.text: Promotion goals set for Black employees; includes a Sponsorship Pilot Program launching in 2024-25 and an EX-02 poster with an organizational need for Indigenous or visible minority candidates.

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals set for racialized employees; includes leveraging non-advertised and acting appointments and a Mentorship Plus program in final development.

inclusion.text: Anti-Racism Action Plan and 2023-2025 Accessibility Plan embedded across the organization; every executive must account for their team's progress in yearly performance evaluations.

progress: Appointed a Director of Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, Accessibility and Anti-Racism in 2023-24, reporting directly to the Chief Commissioner and Executive Director.
Ranked first out of 68 federal departments and agencies in the 2022-2023 Public Service Employee Survey (Hill Times ranking).

PSES Question 23: 89% of all respondents and 77% of racialized respondents feel safe about their career when discussing racism; Question 48: 88% overall and 71% of racialized respondents say the department promotes workplace anti-racism.
Sponsoring an employee of intersectional identity through the Mosaic program; provided appointments and acting positions to several executives who self-identify as Black and/or racialized.
barriers: Limited resources and no additional funding limit data collection, talent management centralization, and learning and training.
Employment equity data must be suppressed for confidentiality given the small population, so representation data is often under-reported.
High volume of corporate reporting requests has put new demands on the Human Resources Division, and central agency delays in a new self-identification system remain a barrier.

organizations.notes: Letter states the Commission was the only public service organization of its size to meet or exceed Government of Canada targets for all employment equity groups in 2020.

letter.author: Catherine MacLeod, for Michael Strong, MD, President
commitments: Established External Advisory Committee on Anti-Racism (July 2021) to co-develop a CIHR anti-racism action plan (planned summer 2022), plus a second advisory stream for Indigenous Peoples.

Planned fall 2021 listening sessions on systemic racism in the health research funding system and an advisory body for persons with disabilities to inform an Accessibility and Anti-Ableism Action Plan.

Revised unconscious bias training module to cover racism, accessibility, systemic ableism, intersectionality and 2SLGBTQIA+ barriers; mandated Anima Leadership anti-racism training for all executives.

Published self-identification data from funding competitions; specialized peer review for Indigenous health research applications; equalized success rates for early career researchers and female applicants.

HR strategy to recruit and retain First Nations, Inuit and Metis employees, including an Employment Systems Review, Mentorship Plus participation and a sourcing/outreach strategy for employment equity groups.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for Indigenous peoples under Strategic Plan 2021-2031 (targeted recruitment, HR strategy to recruit and retain First Nations, Inuit and Metis); specific quantitative targets not yet established.

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goals for Indigenous employees set under the Strategic Plan, without quantitative targets.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals in the Strategic Plan and Accessibility Plan (mental health and well-being, inclusive culture, mandatory training, learning series, engagement), measured via PSES, HR dashboards, Accessibility Progress Report and Employment Equity Reports.

progress: Ran a targeted Indigenous recruitment campaign (external process restricted to Indigenous candidates, Indigenous representation on assessment boards) and volume-managed staffing processes prioritizing persons with disabilities and Indigenous peoples.
Piloted a mentorship program open to all staff; senior leadership supports participation in the Advanced Leadership Pilot Program for Black and Indigenous leaders.
Established External Advisory Committees on Accessibility and Systemic Ableism to co-develop an anti-ableist action plan; held Anti-Black Racism Dialogue in the health research funding system.
Progress tracked via bi-annual dashboards, annual Action Plan, 'Count Yourself In' self-identification campaign and Employment Equity Action Plan (due end of 2024-25).
barriers: No defined quantitative targets for hiring across entry, mid and executive levels, hindering prioritization of focus areas.
Progress communication to employees is weak; need for channels beyond website publication or routine emails.
Time constraints for interest groups balancing committee work with daily tasks, and absence of a clear Champion, hinder buy-in; some employees hesitant to voice experiences.

organizations.notes: Letter reports representation gaps but states no numeric targets: Indigenous 1.5% vs workforce availability 3.2%; visible minorities 17.7% vs 23.4%; persons with disabilities 2.8% vs 8.5%.

letter.author: André M. McArdle, Secretary
commitments: Advertise job opportunities externally to widen the candidate pool and require mandatory unconscious-bias training for all hiring managers.
Tailor the Mentoring Program to approach underrepresented employees with potential for career progression.
Review assessment tools with human resources specialists to ensure accessible, fair and bias-free recruitment and assessment processes.
Pair with larger departments for developmental programs and share pools of qualified candidates from designated groups.
Renew the Health Canada Employee Assistance Services and Alternative Dispute Resolution Services agreement for confidential conflict management, ombuds and harassment/violence support.

black_recruitment.text: Recruitment goal set for Black people using workforce availability.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals set; uses human resources administrative data to compare representation of each designated group against workforce availability to identify gaps.

progress: A Black manager participated in the CICS mentorship program in 2022-23; the Deputy Chief Financial Officer (of Indigenous descent) entered the Comptrollership Leadership Development Program in 2023-24.
A Black employee hired casually in 2023-24 was converted to a permanent position through a non-advertised appointment, and was offered French training for a vacant position.
Executives have addressing the staffing gap in their performance management agreements; workforce availability is updated at year-end to assess progress.
barriers: Labour shortage: external staffing processes yield few candidates, with limited opportunity to favour appointment of employees from racialized or other under-represented communities.
Mandated to recruit half its staff from the provinces, but provincial employees cannot access MyGCHR and cannot self-identify in the system, so they are excluded from CICS statistics.
Small size (32 employees) limits management positions and promotion opportunities and makes maintaining employment equity ratios hard.

letter.author: Paula Isaak, President
commitments: Implement the multi-year (2017-23) Inuit Employment Plan for Nunavut, including plain-language and Inuktut job ads, culturally sensitive posters, Inuktut language training and a talent management process for Inuit employees.

Build a comprehensive Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Plan, starting with an Indigenous Strategy Action Plan in spring 2021 and extending best practices from the Nunavut Inuit Employment Plan to other under-represented groups.
Run an annual survey of Inuit staff in Nunavut (100% response rate in the most recent year) and feed results into forward plans.

Lead Pilimmaksaivik, the Federal Centre of Excellence for Inuit Employment in Nunavut, coordinating a government-wide approach under Article 23 of the Nunavut Agreement, including the Inuit Learning and Development Program and the Sivuliqtiunirmut Illinniarniq Leadership Program.
Add wording on workplace accommodations to all letters of offer (spring 2021) and release a Workplace Harassment and Violence Prevention Policy (August 2021).
targets: Build a representative public service in Nunavut of 85% Nunavut Inuit under Article 23 of the Nunavut Agreement (CanNor Inuit representation at 55% in 2020-21).

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Indigenous peoples: multi-year Inuit Employment Plan targeting 85% Nunavut Inuit representation under Article 23 of the Nunavut Agreement (Inuit representation now over 50%); also implementing the 2023-2028 Yukon Representative Public Service Plan (22.3% Indigenous in Yukon).

inclusion.text: Work is underway to set inclusion goals; using Learning Roadmaps with mandatory diversity and inclusion training, Diversity, Inclusion and Accessibility Champions, and a calendar of cultural and religious events.

progress: Inuit representation has risen to over 50% and the agency is updating its Inuit Employment Plan and targets, while Pilimmaksaivik leads the update of the whole-of-government Inuit Employment Plan (2023-2033).

Plain-language job ads, ads translated into Inuktut, Inuktut language training (one Inuk employee completed full-time training in 2023, a second starting fall 2024) and a comprehensive Inuit talent management process.

Sponsorship and leadership development through Sivuliqtiunirmut Ilinniarniq Leadership Training for Inuit candidates, the Mosaic Leadership Development Program and Canada School of Public Service programs.
Quantitative and qualitative diversity goals are in executive performance agreements; Nunavut executives have additional Inuit talent management goals.
Supports the Inuit Employee Network (bi-monthly meetings) and the Kittuaq Network for Inuit employees across the federal government in Nunavut.
barriers: Recruitment and retention competition across the North: territorial governments and the private sector offer more attractive salaries and benefits.
Hard to approve short-term leave for education or language training and to back-fill vacancies in a small agency, leaving positions vacant for the whole leave.
No northern-specific workforce data for underrepresented groups other than Inuit, and small numbers complicate data collection and progress reporting; awaiting modernized self-identification.
Small numbers risk burnout, participation fatigue, tokenism and compromised privacy for employees from underrepresented groups in employee networks.
As a micro-agency it struggles to match the pace and scope of work larger departments can accomplish.

organizations.notes: The agency says it is also focused on recruiting Black and other racialized people (mandatory diversity training for hiring managers) but set no formal recruitment or promotion goals for them in Question 1.

letter.author: Rumina Velshi (title not shown in the letter text)
commitments: Launched three employee-led networks: Black Employees Network, Indigenous Network, and Women in STEM Network.
First government agency to take the BlackNorth pledge against anti-Black systemic racism.
Transformed recruitment tactics to combat barriers to inclusive hiring.
Five key pillars (inclusive leadership, workplace design, diversity and inclusion capability, empowerment and accountability, leadership) and developing reference materials for leaders on EDI.
Diversity and Inclusion Plan 2019-22.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for Indigenous peoples; Employment Equity Hiring Goals 2022-25 aim to align the workforce with National Labour Market Availability.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for racialized people (as 'visible minorities'); Employment Equity Hiring Goals 2022-25 aim to align the workforce with National Labour Market Availability.

inclusion.text: Goals set, measured via PSES (72.3% response rate in 2022-23), pulse surveys, exit and onboarding surveys, Employment Systems Review, and Organizational Health data.

progress: Annual Employment Equity report and Annual Organizational Health report with identity factors; GBA+ lens applied to employee listening.
Six employee networks with dedicated funding from the EDI Hub budget and HRD EDI Hub support.
Executive performance contracts include talent management objectives on diversity in succession planning; executive cadre and pipeline representation monitored.

October 2023 Pulse Survey improvements: diverse workplace 86% to 88%, feel valued 76% to 87%, psychologically healthy 77% to 82%, behave respectfully 88% to 93%, supervisor provides safe space 77% to 91%.
barriers: Small separate agency with limited FTE; must build its own tools (no access to the TBS TAP portal for modernized self-identification).
Delays in self-identification form and direction from central agencies; cannot collect EE data beyond the four designated groups under the Act (no disaggregated Black data).
STEM and nuclear labour market hiring challenges.

organizations.notes: CNSC does not distinguish Black from racialized employees; it uses 'visible minorities'.

letter.author: Ian Scott, Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer, Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission
commitments: Developing an Anti-Racism and Anti-Discrimination (ARAD) Strategy: engagement included 225 survey respondents and 257 participants in an all-staff session (of about 500 employees); all executives completed intercultural competence self-reflection, a group discussion and an unconscious bias workshop; 158 managers and supervisors trained on unconscious bias and micro-aggressions; report of findings and Action Framework to be finalized in fall 2021.
Launched a three-year Employment Equity, Inclusion and Diversity Plan (May 2021) making diversity and unconscious bias training mandatory for all employees and selection board members.
Set annual diversity staffing targets for the CRTC as a whole and for the executive cadre (Annex B), with sector management teams setting their own targets and a staffing plan guide for 2021-2024.

In 2020-21, 35.8% of new employees and 40% of executive appointees were Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees (up 8.9 and 6.7 percentage points); the executive cadre was expected to close its gap by September 1, 2021.
Targeting staffing for the entry-level CO-01 group (over 40% of the workforce) for employment equity groups exclusively.
Working with other organizations to implement Mentorship Plus in Small Departments and Agencies, and conducting an employment systems review informed by the ARAD Strategy.
A communications campaign to explain 'invisible' elements of diversity, such as invisible disabilities, so the workforce is more aware of its own diversity.
targets: CRTC-wide aspirational targets by March 2024: women 55.0% (workforce availability 50.7%), Indigenous peoples 5.0% (2.6%), visible minorities 21.2% (16.7%), persons with disabilities 9.5% (9.2%).
Executive cadre (EX/LC) aspirational targets by March 2024: women 47.2% (17 of 36), Indigenous peoples 8.3% (3), visible minorities 11.1% (4), persons with disabilities 8.3% (3).

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Indigenous peoples: diversity goals set at 2% above workforce availability for the total population and the executive cadre; new representation targets set for 2025-2027.

black_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Black people (same 2% above workforce availability basis); new representation targets for 2025-2027.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for racialized people (same basis).

inclusion.text: Work is underway to set inclusion goals; updating the EDI Plan for 2024-27 with inclusion metrics and targets based on PSES questions, an internal survey and pulse surveys; inclusion metrics to be finalized in 2024; executive performance agreements outline inclusion objectives.

progress: Progress on the persons with disabilities category (the largest representation gap) and improved representation for Black, racialized and Indigenous employees and persons with disabilities in the executive cadre; new representation targets set for 2025-2027.

2024-25 performance cycle: all senior executives reporting to the Chairperson and CEO are expected to sponsor Indigenous and Black and other racialized employees; a Mosaic candidate was nominated in 2023 and enhanced sponsorship and mentorship programs are launching.
The Chairperson is involved in a recruitment initiative targeting Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees in Communications, launching in fall 2024.
Official language training prioritized through an internal Language School, with language training adapted to employment equity group needs, including meeting CBC profiles at supervisory levels.

Champions and networks for Reconciliation, EDI and Accessibility with dedicated funding; events including Black History Month with Bruny Surin, an event with Andrea Menard, neurodiversity awareness and International Women's Day panels.

Anti-racism, equity and inclusion work embedded in the organizational plan; a comprehensive calendar of significant religious, spiritual and cultural periods exists and is being communicated to staff.
barriers: Measuring EDI progress is hard: cultural shifts and behavioural changes are not easily quantified, and employees may hesitate to disclose personal information due to privacy concerns.
Unconscious bias is deeply engrained and can subtly influence hiring, promotions, team dynamics and workplace culture.

organizations.notes: Promotion targets were not yet set; the self-assessment says promotion targets will be added to accompany the 2025-2027 representation targets, with future focus on promotion and retention of Black and racialized employees. A high number of retirements among Indigenous employees over 2021-2024 impacted representation. Indigenous language training is not currently offered.

letter.author: David Vigneault, Director of the Canadian Security Intelligence Service
commitments: Implemented a new Code of Conduct in November 2020, with employees affirming adherence annually.
Commissioned an external review of employment systems, policies and practices to identify barriers, with recommendations expected in Fall 2021.
Developing a Diversity and Inclusion Strategy with employees and an external diversity and inclusion expert.

Implemented an Interim Diversity and Inclusion Recruitment and Selection Strategy in January 2021, including a dedicated competition for Indigenous or visible minority Intelligence Officers, bias-free selection training, and diverse assessment panels.
Director met with over 150 employees who self-identify as Black, Indigenous or People of Colour to learn about their lived experiences, and committed to continuing those meetings.
targets: 30% of executive appointments in 2020/21 were racialized candidates; racialized representation rose from 17.0% in 2018/19 to 18.2% in 2020/21, while Indigenous representation was flat (2.3% to 2.2%).

indigenous_recruitment.text: By 2026/2027, increase Indigenous representation to 3.4% (2022 DEI Strategy, based on Canadian Workforce Availability with more ambitious aims).

racialized_recruitment.text: By 2026/2027, increase visible minority (racialized) representation to 25%; also 8.9% for persons with disabilities and 25% for women in science and technology.

inclusion.text: 2022 DEI Strategy sets 10 commitments to be implemented by 2025/2026, covering representation, reducing bias in policies and selection, outreach, accountability, cultural awareness, Indigenous reconciliation and data-driven goals; internal DEI survey first run summer 2021, to be re-administered every 4-5 years.

progress: Five bi-annual employment equity dashboards published since 2022; Spring 2024 dashboard showed 22% of action plan commitments complete, 38% with significant advancement and 27% initiated (87% actioned).
Since November 2022, hiring managers consult the DEI team for an employment equity gap analysis before publishing any job poster.
Diverse interview panels integrated for executive processes; integrated coaching program launched for all employees.
Director mentors and sponsors Indigenous employees and asked executive team members to sponsor and mentor racialized and Indigenous employees.
barriers: Official language requirements (French essential, English essential, bilingual imperative) screen out diverse candidates, many of whom are in English regions and meet English-essential requirements only.
Employment equity gap analysis relies on Canadian Workforce Availability data from the 2016 census and 2017 Canadian Survey on Disability, which risks inaccurate comparator points and goals.

organizations.notes: No specific promotion goals set; executive-level representation goals set instead. No separate Black goals; Black employees included in visible minority/racialized goals.

letter.author: Lisa Campbell, President; Mary Preville, Vice-President; Luc Brule, Vice-President
commitments: Established dedicated Human Resources Committee (February 2021) and created Strategic Workforce Management Plan and Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan.
2021-2022 performance agreements for staffing managers include objective to close employment equity representation gaps at hiring, measured over three years.
New Guideline on Appointment Processes (June 2021) to facilitate selection of designated group members in advertised and non-advertised processes.
Designated group hiring goals in staffing plans with priority where gaps exist, including for management positions, and diverse selection boards.
Anti-racism and unconscious bias training mandatory for all managers and directors and strongly recommended for all employees.
Sponsor and support Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees and persons with disabilities in leadership development and employment integration programs.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for Indigenous peoples using workforce availability, population data and government-wide/organizational priorities (targeted selection processes, at-level inventories, non-advertised/non-imperative staffing, prioritizing students and language training).

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for racialized people (same measures as Indigenous); professional development program for Indigenous and visible minorities (EX minus 1).

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goals for Indigenous employees (assignment/acting opportunities, professional development program for EX minus 1).

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals for racialized employees (assignment/acting opportunities, Targeted Employment Equity Initiative participants highlighted in succession planning).

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals in yearly objectives: Mentorship+ (21 mentoring, 11 sponsorship participants), Targeted Employment Equity Initiative (cohort 1: 9 participants; cohort 2: 30), in-house training on eliminating systemic barriers, first three-year Accessibility Plan, mandatory inclusive hiring training for managers, selection boards must include at least one EE group member.

progress: Increased representation for racialized people including in leadership/executive positions.

Mentoring+ sponsorship stream offered to 11 participants in 2023-24, 7 from Black and visible minority communities; targeted EE processes in 2023-24 (Pay Advisor, HR Advisor, IT Technician, targeted summer student cohort) produced hires from Indigenous and visible minority groups.
Quantitative goals in performance management agreements; executives had mandatory 2023-24 commitment to mentor in the mentorship/sponsorship program.
Self-Identification/Self-Declaration campaign launched with a new form and training for all employees to remove stigma.
barriers: Smaller agency budget and resource constraints limit the extent and pace of progress.
Working with outdated data (2016 census, 2017 disability survey); no workforce availability data for sub-groups including Black employees and 2SLGBTQIA+ community.

letter.author: France Pégeot, Chair and CEO
commitments: Implement the Action Plan for Equity, Diversity and Inclusion developed with the Committee on Diversity and Inclusion.
Add mandatory training for employees with a completion performance indicator integrated in all managers' and executives' performance agreements.
Move in spring 2022 to a new fully accessible worksite at 60 Laval in Gatineau, targeting Rick Hansen Foundation Gold+ certification.
Increase representation of Indigenous people, visible minorities and persons with disabilities, using larger departments' inventories, pools and programs and external partnerships.
Review staffing processes to determine trends on diversity and inclusion.

indigenous_recruitment.text: By 2026, increase recruitment of Indigenous persons, Black persons and other racialized people to reduce representation gaps, based on new labour market availability data and business needs; a new series of measurable objectives will be specified.

black_recruitment.text: By 2026, increase recruitment of Indigenous persons, Black persons and other racialized people to reduce representation gaps, based on new labour market availability data and business needs.

racialized_recruitment.text: By 2026, increase recruitment of Indigenous persons, Black persons and other racialized people to reduce representation gaps, based on new labour market availability data and business needs.

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goals set under the three-year people management plan; new measurable objectives to be specified.

black_promotion.text: Promotion goals set under the three-year people management plan; new measurable objectives to be specified.

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals set under the three-year people management plan; new measurable objectives to be specified.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals set in the People Management Strategy, EDI action plan and accessibility plan, measured via the Public Service Employee Survey, workforce analysis and a planned pulse survey.

progress: Launched Mentorship Plus (sponsor/protégé pairs); began 2023-24 with a sponsor and a protégé, with an internal pairing for 2024-25 and four other protégés waiting for an external pairing.

Launched an internal selection process targeting self-declared members of the four employment equity designated groups in the National Capital Region; planning an inventory targeting Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities and visible minorities.
Built an inclusive question bank for assessment tools using the bias-mitigation tool; mandatory training completion integrated into performance agreements.
barriers: Small size: the arrival or departure of one employee can change representation rates; staffing and promotional activity is limited.
Temporary budget allocations over several years limit hiring of indeterminate staff, affecting permanent representation.
Self-declaration is optional, so employees may not self-declare at hiring, making representation targets hard to reach; limited internal resources and reliance on partnerships cause delays.

letter.author: Michelaine Lahaie, Chairperson
commitments: Established an Inclusion, Diversity and Equity Advisory Committee (September 2020) to advise the Chairperson and senior management using an intersectional and GBA+ lens.
Called on the government to appoint an Indigenous member and a racialized member to the Commission (Governor-in-Council appointments).
Gives priority to qualified candidates from employment equity groups when staffing; specifically identified Indigenous candidates as a priority for a Senior Policy Advisor position.

Chairperson, senior management, lawyers, investigators and analysts undertook training on racism, reconciliation, equity and inclusion, including The Path, Indigenous Canada, OCAP fundamentals and the Kairos Blanket Exercise.
Continue outreach to First Nations, community groups and organizations representing racialized communities, and explore student engagement to raise awareness of the Commission as an employer.
Commitment to a hybrid work model and telework to remove geographic barriers for candidates outside the National Capital Region.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Indigenous peoples, using hiring tools, social media groups and Federal Student Work Experience Program bridging.

black_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Black people, using hiring tools, social media groups and Federal Student Work Experience Program bridging.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for racialized people, using hiring tools, social media groups and Federal Student Work Experience Program bridging.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals set through the Accessibility Plan, with metrics from the Public Service Employee Survey.

progress: Created an Indigenous Relations unit for targeted Indigenous recruitment and a Partnerships and Engagement unit that prioritizes BIPOC hiring.
Improved internal communications and held Black History Month events through weekly emails.
Made extensive use of gender-based analysis plus (GBA+).
barriers: Micro-agency size and limited resources, with no dedicated individual or team for this work.
Limited financial resources.
Small size prevents Mosaic sponsorship, which requires promoting into an executive position.

organizations.notes: The Commission notes it is a micro-agency of about 70 employees and that small numbers make representation data impractical to report and a privacy risk.

letter.author: Shelly Bruce, Chief
commitments: Established an Assistant Deputy Minister, Senior Advisor for People, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion.

Establishing a Sponsorship Program focused on progression into senior ranks, particularly the Executive group, with Executive Committee members already taking Black and racialized employees as proteges.
Modernizing HR infrastructure and launching Workday for self-identification and disaggregated data, plus an awareness campaign encouraging staff to self-identify.

Established the People Committee chaired by the Chief, with an Advisory sub-group, and equity-deserving and affinity groups (EmbRACE, Women in Cyber and Intelligence, Neurodiversity Community Group, LGBTQ2+ Community Group).
Developing a Framework for Equity, Diversity and Inclusion and Advice and Guidance on Transgender and non-Binary Person Inclusion.
Learning initiatives on racism, homophobia, and antisemitism (Being Black in Canada, National Indigenous Peoples' Day, IDAHOBIT, Holocaust Remembrance Day).

indigenous_recruitment.text: Hiring goals by 2026-27: Indigenous representation 2.26% to 2.52%; goal of 3 of every 4 new hires being an EE group member over 3 years.

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goal: +1.5% Indigenous representation in management roles (2 employees; currently no Indigenous manager or executive).

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goal: +3% racialized employees in senior management roles (4 employees; currently 14% of managers are ethnic minority vs 17% of employees; no Black man in an executive position).

inclusion.text: 10 inclusion criteria developed at a December 2023 symposium (linguistic inclusion, social inclusion, workforce representation, psychological safety, accessibility, inclusive culture, discussions on workplaces and decision making, recognition and advancement, inclusive leadership, sense of belonging and authenticity); methodology to survey the workforce under development.

progress: Dashboards updated monthly and presented to governance committees four times a year; organizational scorecard for 2024-25.
Sponsorship pilot (56 applicants, 14 selected), extended to 24 months from fall 2024, with sponsors expanded from ADMs to directors.
12 funded affinity groups; mandatory organizational EDI commitment in all employees' performance agreements.
barriers: Insufficient communication and resistance, including perceptions of advantage and tokenism; EDI fatigue.
Tokenism side effects of quantifiable measures.
Self-identification questionnaire split in two; the second (disaggregated, including Black) gets few responses.
Workforce shortages in IT and cyber plus a rigorous security process; need more resources for harassment, racism, labour relations, and accessibility case management.

organizations.notes: No separate Black goals: the self-identification questionnaire is split in two and the second disaggregated questionnaire, including Black, gets few responses.

letter.author: Nathalie Théberge, Vice President and CEO
commitments: Joined the 50-30 Challenge on December 15, 2020 (gender parity and 30% representation of other under-represented groups on boards and senior management).

Added mandatory training (Values and Ethics, harassment and violence prevention, respectful workplace) to all employees' performance agreements in 2020-21, with unconscious bias and diversity training added in 2021-22.
Signed an agreement with Health Canada for employee access to Ombuds services and informal conflict resolution support.
Established an Employee Workplace Wellness Committee (2020-21) with a mandate covering diversity and inclusion awareness.
Undertook a comprehensive review of internal policies (staffing, training, performance agreements) to ensure they are inclusive and free of systemic barriers.
Secretary General signed the Heads of Human Resources Statement of Action Against Systemic Racism, Bias and Discrimination (December 4, 2020).
targets: 50-30 Challenge: 50% gender parity and 30% representation of other under-represented groups (including racialized people, persons with disabilities, LGBTQ2) on boards and senior management teams.

progress: Seven secondments and acting secondments since 2019 for Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees, occasionally leading to promotional appointments.
Exploring earmarking two positions (one legal expert, one leadership) for recruitment and development of Indigenous, Black and other racialized people.
Uses the Innovation, Science and Economic Development equity, diversity and inclusion calendar and online resources through a service agreement.
barriers: Micro-organization of fewer than 25 employees: representation numbers can swing from 100% to 0%, and standard initiatives such as employment equity talent pools are not sustainable.
Positions require specialized legal or economic expertise plus bilingualism, sharply limiting the available candidate pool.
Treasury Board employee data does not reflect secondments and acting secondments, which are the Board's main path for recruiting and developing equity-seeking employees.
No formal measures to assess progress, no sponsorship approach, and no accountability approach in performance management yet.

organizations.notes: No recruitment, promotion or inclusion goals set yet in the self-assessment (work underway on all).
