Set local representation objectives for Indigenous peoples and visible minorities that exceed workforce availability, based on offender representation at each location.
Launch a Sponsorship program in fall 2021 and review the National Mentorship program to identify and reduce barriers for underrepresented groups.

Formalized a Statement on Diversity, Equity and Inclusion in the Workplace signed by all senior executive committee members, with a diversity and inclusion performance objective for every executive, manager and supervisor.
Conduct an Audit of Culture to examine all dimensions of organizational culture.
Launched the National Comprehensive Strategy on Workplace Wellness and Employee Wellbeing in 2020, with annual reporting on workplace climate.
targets: Representation objectives for Indigenous peoples and visible minorities exceeding workforce availability, set per unit using 30% offender representation plus 70% regional workforce availability.
Meet workforce availability for women and persons with disabilities by 2025.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Work underway to set goals; location-specific representation objectives (70% workforce availability plus 30% offender representation) are published on an intranet dashboard, but no hiring objectives for Indigenous workers because there is no national representation gap.

black_recruitment.text: No workforce availability data exists for Black employees, so no goals set; comparative analysis of the Black workforce (pay, age, occupational groups) is underway.

racialized_recruitment.text: Work underway to set goals; location-specific representation objectives (70% workforce availability plus 30% offender representation) are published on an intranet dashboard, but no hiring objectives for racialized workers because there is no national representation gap.

inclusion.text: Work underway to set goals; a Maturity Model on Diversity and Inclusion self-assessment is planned for fiscal year 2024-2025 to establish a baseline, and a National Working Group is being established to build a performance measurement framework.

progress: Established a National Working Group with regional representatives, subject matter experts and representatives from equity-deserving groups to co-design multi-year hiring and promotion goals and a performance measurement framework.

Assistant Commissioner / Regional Deputy Commissioner performance measures for 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 require sponsoring at least two Indigenous, Black or other racialized employees; almost all Executive Committee members have identified proteges.
Recorded an Indigenous recruitment endorsement video in Spring 2024 and started a process to recruit Black and other racialized applicants for the Atlantic Region.
Prioritized second language training for employment equity and equity-seeking employees through a June 2023 memorandum to executives.
barriers: Statistics Canada census data does not reflect current workforce availability, which affects the representation objective formula and targeted hiring and promotion.
Delays in self-identification modernization limit the ability to collect accurate self-identification data and measure progress.
Employees find dialogue about equity and racism challenging, particularly when it calls on individuals to reflect on past experiences or sympathize with unfamiliar barriers.

letter.author: Darlene H. Carreau, Chief Administrator
commitments: Approved and implemented FACES: Anti-Racism Strategy 2020-2025 (August 2020); appointed an Anti-Racism Champion and established the Chief Administrator Anti-Racism Consultation Group and Action Committee (26 members, meeting quarterly).
Developed a Safe Space Policy (to be tabled for approval September 2021) and a Mandate Letter/Membership Participation Agreement for the committee.
Delivered mandatory anti-racism community dialogue sessions for employees and managers, plus Black History Month, Indigenous Heritage Month, Asian Heritage Month and Pride speaker series.
Drafted a Diversity and Inclusion Plan with objectives and indicators; 5-year Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan to be finalized and implemented.
Prioritize Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees and employees with disabilities for upcoming executive vacancies and sponsor high-potential employees through leadership development.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for Indigenous peoples under the 2023-26 Employment Equity Plan: eliminate underrepresentation vs workforce availability rates (short-term quantitative goals), plan over-representation to mitigate departures.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for racialized people under the 2023-26 Employment Equity Plan (same WFA-based goals).

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goals for Indigenous employees: representation rates used as goals where at/above WFA; WFA rates used where underrepresented.

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals for racialized employees (same WFA-based approach).

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals in the 2022-25 Diversity and Inclusion Strategic Plan: promote a culture of inclusion and belonging; build, develop and retain a diverse and inclusive workforce; embed D&I in practices, policies and programs; measured via PSES, exit interviews and D&I training completion.

progress: Employment Systems Review completed and hiring processes reviewed to be barrier-free; Diversity, Inclusion and Anti-racism Team established (May 2022).

D&I, anti-racism and EE commitments embedded in all executives' performance agreements, with indicators (achieve EE representation goals, bias-free postings/tools/interviews); corporate priority 'Our People' added in 2023-24.
Deputy head personally endorsed promotional appointments of Indigenous, Black and racialized employees; all competition posters state selection may be limited to EE designated groups.
Enhanced culture of awareness and transparency: employees more empowered to call out discrimination; PSES and promotion/retention data shared by EE group.
barriers: Small organization with limited managerial and executive positions; lack of advancement opportunities makes retention of EE group talent hard against larger departments.
Self-identification data voluntary and unreliable; some employees fear stigmatization and prejudice; data tied to pay file transfers so rarely up to date.

commitments: Establish an independent Ombudsperson office by March 31, 2022 to track, report and resolve harassment and discrimination.
Require 15 hours of mandatory Indigenous cultural competency learning per employee per year under the Indigenous Cultural Competency Learning Policy.
Adopt the Mentorship Plus program and launch the first intake; join the Indigenous Management Development Program with ISC, Health Canada, PHAC and CFIA.
Deliver 40 Positive Space sessions by end of December 2021 (17 held as of August 2021) and support the Two-Spirit and LGBTQQIA+ network in implementing the LGBT Purge Fund report recommendations.
Review the Staffing Framework to add a module on recruiting and retaining Indigenous employees and develop a comprehensive action plan on identifying, removing and preventing barriers to inclusion.
Hold senior managers accountable to answer three questions on who is missing from decision-making, who is not attracted or retained, and what makes it difficult for them to stay.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Department-wide five-year workforce diversity recruitment goals for each employment equity group, including Indigenous people and visible minorities (Black and racialized people), until 2027, re-evaluated annually, based on mandate, operational priorities and workforce availability.

black_recruitment.text: Five-year recruitment goals for each employment equity group, including visible minorities (Black and racialized people), until 2027, re-evaluated annually.

racialized_recruitment.text: Five-year recruitment goals for each employment equity group, including visible minorities (Black and racialized people), until 2027, re-evaluated annually.

progress: Created an Ombuds Office (August 2023) focused on hearing from marginalized groups and making independent recommendations to senior management.

Sponsored two Indigenous employees through the Mosaic Leadership Development program; each executive's performance agreement requires supporting at least one Indigenous, Black, racialized or disabled person for a leadership role.

Ran targeted Indigenous recruitment processes (EX-01 and EX-03; CR-04/CR-05/AS-01 collective inventories; EC-03/04/05 directories) and launched the Indigenous Cousin System pilot and Senior Management Twinning Program.

Offers the Official Languages Training Program for Indigenous Employees annually; hiring diversity goals tracked quarterly and executives assessed on diversity, inclusion and anti-racism objectives at mid-year and year-end.
barriers: Retention is a challenge; official-language skills required for management and executive positions are a barrier for Indigenous employees.
Consultation and engagement processes can be laborious and confusing; a need for champions in areas such as accessibility emerged.
Lack of training to understand and measure the issues (unconscious bias, cultural competence, positive space).

commitments: Developed an Anti-Racism Action Plan through the grassroots Anti-Racism Collective (40 volunteers), unanimously endorsed by the Executive Committee, including a mentorship and sponsorship program and culturally sensitive talent and performance management.
Required all executives to complete anti-racism and unconscious bias training (W005) by March 31, 2021.
Applied an unconscious-bias lens to University Recruitment; 80% of 2020-21 new hires self-identified with at least one equity-seeking group.
Created an Anti-Racism Ambassadors network in each branch.
Held difficult conversations after the murder of George Floyd, anti-Asian violence and revelations about residential schools.

commitments: Established an Anti-Racism and Anti-Discrimination Secretariat (November 2020) and an Anti-Racism and Anti-Discrimination Results Framework (approved April 15, 2021) built on representation, career development, anti-racism training and culture change, and measurement and leadership accountability.

Mentorship and sponsorship program for Indigenous, Black, other racialized groups and persons with disabilities, with EX 1-3 and LC 1-3 executives sponsored by EX 4-level sponsors.

All EX/LC performance management agreements (2021-22 and beyond) include specific targeted actions; assistant deputy ministers must justify decisions where employment equity candidates are not selected at EX minus 2 and above.

Sponsorship pilot with 22 sponsorship relationships; targeted departmental Sponsorship Program being developed (Indigenous, Black, racialized, SOGIE, persons with disabilities).
Targeted LC-01 recruitment process open only to Indigenous candidates (launched April 2023, 100% representative board); LC-02 process with cascading area of selection and prequalified pool (2022).

Fear of reprisal resulting in a complaint-averse culture; need for trauma-informed, culturally competent complaint processes.

Annex B baseline (2020-21 executive appointments): 0 Indigenous, 1 Black, 3 other racialized out of 24; Black recruitment fell to 9 hires from 24 in 2019-20.

Partner with Indigenous peoples to develop an Indigenous learning curriculum (Truth and Reconciliation Commission Call to Action 57).

Low self-identification completion rates, and limits in the current self-identification form, with the new Treasury Board form delayed.

Implement the Indigenous Recruitment and Retention Strategy, Inuit Employment Plan and Accessibility Strategy, and create an implementation taskforce to monitor progress.

Inclusive talent management with employment equity as a criterion for development and training nominations, and participation in the Small Departments and Agencies group exploring Mentorship+ for Indigenous, Black and racialized employees.

Learning: unconscious bias training completed by 100% of executives and nearly 80% of staff, plus workshops with Ryerson University's Diversity Institute, an Open Staff Dialogue with the Federal Black Employee Caucus and other learning events.

Undertook a review of human resources and recruiting policies to identify barriers, including a Policy on Accommodation in consultation stage.
Develop a 2021-2024 Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion action plan and initiate an employment systems review in 2021-2022.
Used targeted recruiting and a hybrid office model to widen the candidate pool, with staffing posters indicating Indigenous or visible minority candidates may be considered before others.

progress: 13 appointment processes targeted employment equity groups in 2023-2024, and 83% of new hires and deployed employees self-identified as belonging to one or more employment equity groups.

letter.author: Sarah Paquet, Director and Chief Executive Officer
commitments: Joined ISED 50-30 Challenge to improve access to leadership for women, racialized persons including Black Canadians, LGBTQ2 people, persons with disabilities and First Nations, Inuit and Metis peoples.
Chief Human Resources Officer Karen Figuerola took the EEDI Champion role and signed the Statement of Action Against Systemic Racism, Bias, and Discrimination.
Implementing a new Human Capital Management system under the Digital Strategy for improved EEDI data and reporting, plus a self-identification campaign aligned with OCHRO modernization.
Adopted Panel Pledge 2.0 to increase representation of Black and racialized Canadians, persons with disabilities, Indigenous peoples and LGBTQ2 people on government panels and events.
Neurodiversity recruitment initiative with Specialisterne and the Office of Public Service Accessibility.

Modernized Staffing and Talent Acquisition Policy Suite (June 2021) requiring employment equity considerations in HR plans and staffing strategies, removing preference for Canadian citizens and using plain, inclusive language.
Adopting Mentorship Plus (adding a sponsorship component) to the existing mentorship program for under-represented and equity-seeking groups.

Accountability through concrete objectives in performance management agreements: by end of 2021-22 all management levels report on leading anti-racism and barrier work, promoting inclusion learning, and targeted recruitment of employment equity groups.
Enhanced reporting and dashboards from the new Human Capital Management system to monitor tangible results on representation and inclusion.
targets: 50-30 Challenge: 50% women and 30% other equity-deserving groups in senior management and on boards (joined the Challenge)

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals for racialized employees under the same three-year approach.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals for 2023-24 to 2025-26 in the EEDI Strategy: close representation gaps vs workforce availability, improve PSES results (anti-racism, psychologically healthy workplace, job fit and development, discrimination, harassment), robust participation in D&I learning paths.

progress: Launched Mentorship Plus first cohort in 2022 (senior executives sponsor proteges); partnered with With You With Me (2022-23) for potential-based hiring of Indigenous, disability and women-in-STEM talent, with several hires underway.
Modernized self-identification questionnaire launched summer 2023 with Workday HCM system, enabling real-time disaggregated data; established internal Language School.
Corporate EEDI commitment in every leader's performance agreement, assessed in calibration and influencing final ratings; talent management incorporates EE data and 50-30 Challenge objectives.
EEDI working group membership doubled over five years; partnered with Coalition of Innovation Leaders Against Racism (CILAR) as an Activator since November 2022.
barriers: Previous HR system limited data analytics; building reporting dashboards and analytical tools remains a priority.
Voluntary self-identification data: small numbers for specific equity sub-groups raise confidentiality and representativeness concerns in a small agency.
Reporting burden: annual EE, Multiculturalism, Call to Action, Accessibility Plan, Pay Equity and ad-hoc reports strain small-agency resources.

letter.author: Timothy Sargent, Deputy Minister
commitments: Set annual recruitment goals under the Talent Acquisition Framework to meet representation objectives over the next four years, monitoring hires, departures and promotions of employment equity groups.
Launch the National Indigenous Recruitment, Retention and Development Strategy and Action Plan and a Surge Staffing Team for employment-equity-focused hiring.
Participate in the Treasury Board Secretariat Mentorship+ Learning Lab with a sponsorship focus; nearly two dozen participants selected from employment equity groups.
Have the executive cadre complete three Canada School of Public Service unconscious-bias courses (99% completion rate).
Develop 302 talent management plans by end of fiscal year 2020-21, 241 of them targeting members of employment equity groups.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for Indigenous people based on current representation vs Treasury Board Secretariat workforce availability and anticipated turnover; aim to meet workforce availability at all levels.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for racialized people based on current representation vs workforce availability and anticipated turnover.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals being set for 2024-25 through the Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan; KPIs include increasing representation vs workforce availability, external employment equity appointments, self-identification completion, employment equity promotions, developmental opportunities, sponsorship participants and employment equity employee satisfaction in the Public Service Employee Survey.

progress: Adopted an employment-equity-first approach to staffing (September 2023): 111 employment equity appointments made via National Talent Acquisition services identifying 1,813 employment equity candidates; justification required where appointees are not employment equity members.

DFO/Canadian Coast Guard Sponsorship Program delivered three cohorts; third cohort (2023-24) had 19 protégés (3 Indigenous, 5 racialized) and three protégés from earlier cohorts have been promoted into the Executive cadre.
Self-identification awareness campaign in 2023 raised employee engagement 5% (to 85%); quarterly EEDI KPI dashboard and Power BI dashboards track representation, promotions and attrition.
Launched racialized and women+ employee networks in early 2024; Indigenous Career Navigators (14 trained volunteers) support Indigenous employees, candidates and hiring managers.
barriers: Decentralized workforce (400+ locations, many staff on ships and research vessels) makes inclusive engagement and consultation hard.
Operational and bona fide requirements (sea-going posts, remote lightkeeper stations, costly marine certifications) make closing representation gaps for persons with disabilities hard.

Attitudinal barriers: the 2023-24 Ombuds report showed a widespread lack of bystander/upstander behaviour; 2022 Public Service Employee Survey showed elevated sexism and ableism; the Employment Systems Review cited toxic workplace culture and lack of trust in management.
No workforce availability benchmark for Black representation exists yet to guide recruitment or promotion goals.

commitments: Launched a departmental anti-racism strategy and action plan in fall 2021, including a Deputy Minister Pilot Sponsorship Program, anti-racism training and labour market availability-grounded benchmarks.
Created an Anti-racism Secretariat reporting to an assistant deputy minister, with an environmental scan and an inaugural annual anti-racism survey.
Built an anti-racism learning pathway, including an executive course and online training for all employees.
Developed an Action Plan on Reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples 2021-2025.

Set labour market availability-grounded representation benchmarks at all levels, including senior managerial and head of mission positions, and launched the Deputy Minister Pilot Sponsorship Program in autumn 2021.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Indigenous peoples for 2023-24 and beyond, to close gaps and meet workforce availability targets.

black_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Black people for 2023-24 and beyond, to close gaps and meet workforce availability targets.

progress: Nine graduates of the first Deputy Minister Sponsorship Program joined the executive ranks by end of 2023; a second cohort of 15 participants began in November 2023.

Made the Anti-Racism Secretariat permanent in September 2022; representation improved in head of mission appointments and the executive cadre.
Developed the Anti-Racism and Diversity Impact Assessment Tool and dashboards.
barriers: Departure rates for Indigenous, Black and visible minority employees remain a concern, especially in the executive cadre.

letter.author: Stephen Lucas, Deputy Minister; Dr. Harpreet Kochhar, Associate Deputy Minister
commitments: Held Anti-Racism Listening Sessions (fall 2020) with independent facilitators and is acting on their recommendations: customized language training, a review of HR practices for unconscious bias, psychological safety, and cultural sensitivity training.

Strengthened and funded employee networks (Black Employees Matter Network created February 2021, Indigenous Employees Network, Visible Minorities, Gender and Sexual Diversity, Persons with Disabilities, Managers and Young Professionals networks, over 1,700 members), with ADM champions and network work recognized in performance agreements.

Launched the Leadership Council on Diversity and Inclusion (summer 2020), chaired by the Deputy Minister and Associate Deputy Minister, to co-develop strategies on inclusive staffing, unconscious bias and diverse selection boards.

Created an Executive Level Indigenous Inventory, hiring four self-identified Indigenous executives since 2020, plus the Indigenous Management Development Program and Indigenous Career Management for Employees Program; formalized pools of Indigenous, Black and racialized candidates for executive roles.
Launched the Equitable Access to Language Training Program (March 2021) for employment equity groups; 123 employees had joined.

Introduced Mentorship Plus for high-potential Indigenous, Black and racialized employees, diverse selection boards, manager training on unconscious bias in staffing, and a Practical Guide for Managers on Inclusive Recruiting.

Created a Diversity and Inclusion Office with a Network Secretariat and an Anti-Racism and Anti-Discrimination Team, both led by senior racialized leaders; publishes Employment Equity Workforce Demographic Reports on the intranet and launched a 2021 Self-Identification Campaign.

Anti-Racist Science Action Plan (launch fall 2021) to eradicate racial bias in science, and an Employment Systems Review in 2021 to inform the 2022-2025 Multi-Year Diversity and Employment Equity Plan.

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals for Black, Indigenous, and racialized employees discussed October 2023; calculating promotion goals for all EE groups for 2024-25.

progress: Data Hub (fall 2023) with real-time disaggregated EE data via Power BI (branch, directorate, occupational group, EX/non-EX).

Mentorship Plus with 178 mentees and 188 mentors, all matched as of June 2024; Indigenous Recruitment Team (2021) and Black, Racialized and Equity Deserving Communities (BREDC) recruitment team (early 2023).
Indigenous Qualified and 'At Level' Talent Pool (June 2024); 2-3 advertised processes open to Indigenous peoples in 2024-25; Black and Racialized Career Advancement Strategy endorsed fall 2023.

Restoring Indigenous representation and cultural competency after the transfer of the First Nations and Inuit Health Branch to Indigenous Services Canada.

PSES 2020: 12% of Indigenous and 10% of racialized respondents reported harassment (vs 8% for others); 10% of racialized respondents reported discrimination (vs 4%).

commitments: Established the Chairperson's Advisory Committee on Diversity and Inclusion (fall 2020) and released the IRB's first Diversity and Inclusion Strategic Plan (three pillars, with performance measures).
Made unconscious bias and anti-racism training mandatory for leaders, with wider rollouts planned across the organization.
Appointed the IRB's first Ombudsperson in 2020 to promote a healthy, diverse and inclusive workplace.
Review staffing processes and tools with the Public Service Commission's Personnel Psychology Centre to identify and remove barriers.

Publish revised Chairperson's Guidelines on Gender and on Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, and Sex Characteristics by end of calendar year, plus trauma-informed decision-making guidance; train decision-makers on avoiding unconscious bias early in 2022.
Establish a talent recruitment and retention plan, publish a hiring manager's toolkit, and launch sponsorship and leadership development programs for under-represented groups.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Annual recruitment and staffing goals set under the Diversity and Inclusion Strategic Plan, revised each year on Treasury Board workforce availability estimates, considering underrepresentation by occupational classification, attrition and planned staffing.

racialized_recruitment.text: Annual recruitment and staffing goals set under the Diversity and Inclusion Strategic Plan, revised each year on Treasury Board workforce availability estimates (Black and racialized combined).

inclusion.text: 2024-2026 Diversity and Inclusion Strategic Plan sets four goals (promote a diverse and inclusive culture; build a representative workforce; embed diversity and inclusion in policies and programs; measure progress and hold ourselves accountable) with 24 initiatives to complete by March 31, 2026.

progress: Reports semi-annually to management on employment equity representation versus workforce availability estimates and staffing targets.

Mentorship Plus Program paired 17 employment equity group employees with 17 executives; two employees sponsored to the Mosaic Leadership Development Program, one of whom graduated in 2023 and was appointed to an executive position.
Developing a Performance Measurement Framework for the 2024-2026 plan, with progress reported twice a year to the Executive Committee and the Chairperson's Advisory Committee.
Representation and inclusion objectives integrated into the Executive Talent Management System.
barriers: Obtaining accurate data on employment equity groups: over 88% of employees have self-identified but a fully accurate picture is still lacking; awaiting the new Government of Canada self-identification campaign.
No workforce availability estimates for Black people, so no separate Black goals can be set.
Almost 50% of the workforce is in determinate positions on temporary funding, making retention of diverse recruits difficult (from the 2021 letter).

organizations.notes: No numeric representation targets in the letter (Annex A commits to setting annual appointment targets but states no figures). No promotion goals and no separate Black goals in the self-assessment.

letter.author: Catrina Tapley, Deputy Minister; Caroline Xavier, Associate Deputy Minister; Scott Jones, Associate Deputy Minister
commitments: Created the Anti-Racism Task Force in summer 2020 with 12 full-time equivalents and $4 million in funding from July 2021 to July 2024.
Published an Anti-Racism Value Statement acknowledging the department's lasting impact on Indigenous, Black and racialized peoples.
Launched a department-wide Anti-Racism Survey in November 2020 to establish baseline disaggregated data, and created trust circles for racialized employees.

Set Anti-Racism Sector Commitments with tangible actions for each business line over three years and added anti-racism, equity and inclusion objectives to all executives' performance management agreements.
Implemented a Racial Impact Assessment Tool for policy-making and updated the Newcomer Outcomes Survey to obtain race-based data.
Revised the Oath of Citizenship to recognize Indigenous Peoples and their treaty rights, fulfilling Truth and Reconciliation Commission Call to Action 94.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Employment equity representation baseline objectives endorsed October 2021 (three-year commitment), based on labour market availability rather than workforce availability, with disaggregated data for Black employees; baselines are a floor, not a ceiling (specific numeric baselines not stated in the response).

black_recruitment.text: Employment equity representation baseline objectives endorsed October 2021 (three-year commitment), based on labour market availability rather than workforce availability, with disaggregated data for Black employees; baselines are a floor, not a ceiling (specific numeric baselines not stated in the response).

racialized_recruitment.text: Employment equity representation baseline objectives endorsed October 2021 (three-year commitment), based on labour market availability rather than workforce availability, with disaggregated data for Black employees; baselines are a floor, not a ceiling (specific numeric baselines not stated in the response).

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goals set for Indigenous employees within the employment equity representation baseline objectives.

black_promotion.text: Promotion goals set for Black employees within the employment equity representation baseline objectives.

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals set for racialized employees within the employment equity representation baseline objectives.

inclusion.text: Anti-Racism Strategy 2.0 (2021-2024) with an Accountability and Transparency Framework and measurable goals; a multi-year Anti-Racism, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (ARDEI) People Management Plan is in development, with an ARDEI Index pilot to measure executive performance on ARDEI commitments.

progress: Employment equity representation increased at all career levels, tracked through a monthly EE Status Report Tool with disaggregated data and a weekly HR Dashboard available to all employees.
Created the Equity Branch in October 2023 as a centre of equity expertise, plus an Employee Support Office and a planned Ombuds Office.
Made unconscious bias training mandatory for all employees and conducted an Employment Systems Review and focus groups (Pollara, 2021 and 2023).
Improved the EE Status Report Tool to include measurable targets toward increasing representation of all employment equity groups at all career levels by the end of 2024.
barriers: Funding constraints limit the ability to advance diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives, hire external experts, or invest in necessary resources.
Competing priorities and the need for alignment at all levels, plus an October 2023 organizational realignment, caused change management and survey fatigue.
Lack of awareness and trust in the self-identification process may be preventing a true portrait of the department's diversity, and there is a lack of representation at senior management levels.

organizations.notes: Letter states new baseline targets for a representative workforce were to be established by end of 2021 (process commitment, not a numeric target).

letter.author: David McGovern
commitments: Developed three-year Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan with over 30 actions on representation, combatting racism and bias, and education and awareness.
Created Indigenous Employees' Circle and networks for visible minorities, women, LGBTQ+, allies and persons with disabilities.
Fully implemented Mentorship Plus program (three mentors and three mentees).
Created an application inventory for equity-deserving candidates already qualified in other employment pools and used targeted external pools.
President and entire executive team signed an Anti-Racism Pledge; mandatory EEDI training for senior management on inclusive leadership and unconscious bias.
Made equity-deserving groups a priority group for the Official Languages Training Program; EEDI lens to be applied to review of programs including the talent placement program for non-executives.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for Indigenous peoples: ambitious hiring targets set at workforce availability +1% from 2023-2024, tracked via quarterly dashboards.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals for racialized people: hiring targets at workforce availability +1% from 2023-2024, tracked via quarterly dashboards.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals in the completed three-year EDI action plan and EEDI Evergreen Action Plan (leader accountability, cultural competence, combatting bias/racism/discrimination); 63 internal articles and 25 events; Indigenous Career Navigator hired; Tool for Mitigating Biases and Barriers in Assessments implemented.

progress: Successfully achieving representation goals for racialized and Indigenous peoples; meets representation targets in three of four equity groups (gap remains for persons with disabilities).
Hired an Indigenous candidate for an executive position via targeted selection; welcomed an Indigenous Career Navigator on deployment.
Language training program prioritizes Indigenous, Black and racialized employees and removes the need to self-identify to access it (since fall 2023).
Sponsored one employee through the Mosaic Leadership Development program; EDI Evergreen Action Plan produced 63 internal articles and 25 events.
barriers: EEDI work is led by committee volunteers with full-time jobs, creating resource constraints on pace and depth.
Some employees fatigued with EEDI discussions; efforts risk being treated as a compliance 'check-the-box' exercise.

Official Languages Act requirements can pose barriers (e.g., racialized employees learning a third/fourth language; asking Indigenous employees to learn official languages can be seen as colonization); identifying Black and 2SLGBTQIA+ representation is a data challenge.

letter.author: Christiane Fox, Deputy Minister, and Valerie Gideon, Associate Deputy Minister
commitments: Implement a mandatory Indigenous Cultural Competency Learning Policy requiring 15 hours of culturally competent learning per employee per year, with a baseline survey repeated on a cyclical basis.
Create a rotational assignment opportunity in the Deputy Minister's Office (up to 6 months) for Indigenous employees at EX minus 1, 2 or 3, with Assistant Deputy Minister offices doing the same.

Create a Task Force on Diversity and Inclusion, Equity, and Anti-Racism of employee networks reporting to a Deputy Minister/Associate Deputy Minister co-chaired Leadership Council on Diversity and Inclusion, Equity, and Anti-Racism.

Pilot an EX-04/EX-05 staffing process co-developing competencies reflecting Indigenous values with an inclusive selection board including Indigenous partners; assess employment equity group members first in a current EX-03 process.
Revise the Staffing Framework (January 2020) to include an Indigenous recruitment and retention module and use collective and specific staffing processes tailored to recruiting Indigenous employees.
Treat workforce availability estimates as the floor, not the ceiling, and hold a discussion on representation targets in early fall.

Adopt the Treasury Board Secretariat Mentorship Plus program, matching members of designated employment equity and other underrepresented communities with executive mentors and sponsors, with a first intake in the coming months.

Create an Ombudsperson Office to help employees navigate systems and provide impartial advice and upward feedback on systemic issues, and a Respect Charter co-developed with union representatives (to be endorsed in fall 2021).

Workforce availability estimates are the floor, not the ceiling; three guiding principles set by the Leadership Council on Diversity and Inclusion, Equity and Anti-Racism (diverse and representative workforce; equitable, inclusive, accessible and welcoming environment; equal and equitable access to resources and opportunities).

Created a GBA Plus Responsibility Centre and community of practice, informed by the Indigenous Women's Well-Being Advisory Committee, and an Indigenous Employee Secretariat (shared with CIRNAC) supporting First Nations, Inuit and Metis employees.
targets: March 31, 2021 baseline (Annex C): women 68.6% (workforce availability 66.2%), Indigenous peoples 27.2% (5.5%), persons with disabilities 5.3% (8.9%), visible minorities 15.6% (16.2%). In 2020-21, of 693 hires: 95 Indigenous (13.7%), 21 Black (3.0%), 65 racialized (9.4%); of 16 non-EX to EX appointments: 0 Black; of 14 EX to EX appointments: 0 Black and 0 racialized.

black_recruitment.text: Five-year recruitment goals for each employment equity group, including visible minorities (Black and racialized people), until 2027, re-evaluated annually.

black_recruitment.text: 2023-24 recruitment target: 47 Black people (achieved 84, 178%).

racialized_recruitment.text: 2023-24 recruitment target: 215 racialized people (achieved 284, 132%).

inclusion.text: S.M.A.R.T. inclusion goals in the triennial Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan (2022-2025) under four pillars (Training and Awareness, Staffing, Talent Management, Accountability), measured via event attendance, network membership growth, training completion, Public Service Employee Survey results, drop-off rates, exit surveys and promotion/departure rates.

progress: Met 2023-24 departmental recruitment targets: Indigenous 35 of 31 (113%), racialized 284 of 215 (132%), Black 84 of 47 (178%).

Third cohort of the Sponsorship Program has 10 ongoing sponsorship relationships (1 Black, 1 person with disability, 5 racialized, 8 women); Aspiring Leader Program cohort (January 2024) has 30 participants, 50% from equity groups.
Implemented an Inclusion Steward initiative in performance and talent review panels; increased funding to diversity networks to $15,000 per network as of 2023.
Created a Duty to Accommodate Centre of Expertise (2023) and a OneHR dashboard; Ombuds report on lived experiences of equity-identifying employees used alongside quantitative data.
barriers: Access to timely demographic and intersectional data is limited (census blocks, no 2SLGBTQIA+ data except biennial Public Service Employee Survey, delayed self-identification modernization); data literacy gaps.
Engagement vs communication: prescriptive government communication and information overload make trust-based engagement for cultural change hard.

Mental health: lack of explicit direction on what is expected of mental health programs in advancing the Call to Action and where responsibilities of mental health, occupational health and safety and EDI teams begin and end.

commitments: Developed an action plan to counter systemic anti-Black racism with short-, medium- and long-term deliverables, guided by an Anti-Black Racism working group (November 2020) and an Advisory Committee to Address Anti-Black Racism (May 2021, 11 Black researchers).
Boosted employment equity recruitment through targeted staffing, diversified senior management and created a Manager of Equity, Diversity and Inclusion position.
Created an Office of the Ombuds and Well-Being Services (four staff) and a Persons with Disabilities Network (June 2021).
Launched the Race, Gender and Diversity Initiative ($12 million, Budget 2021).
Finalized a People Strategy informed by the Culture Audit and explored Mentorship Plus.
targets: Equity and diversity targets for the Canada Research Chairs Program to meet Canada's projected 2029 population (specific numbers not stated).

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set for Indigenous peoples; short-term representation goals for 2024-27 using National Capital Region labour market availability, aiming to close gaps in years 1-3 and exceed targets in years 4-5.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals set, included in 2024-25 performance management agreements for all levels.

progress: The Mentorship Plus pilot in 2023-24 surpassed its target for mentor/mentee connections.
Communicated representation goals for 2024-27 to all staff and included them in performance management agreement templates.
Runs an in-house Language Training Program prioritizing employment equity groups since 2022, with weekly one-to-one and small-group tutoring to B/C levels.
Adopted collaboration principles for employee-led equity groups, with chairs in the Employment Equity and Diversity Advisory Committee; published a guide on cultural and religious dates.

First year of the forward direction: increased awareness and inclusion (employee-led equity groups as safer spaces), enhanced collaboration and engagement through a strengthened Employment Equity and Diversity Advisory Committee, and improved transparency and accountability from open dialogue on the internal cultural and employment systems review and representation and inclusion commitments in performance management agreements.
barriers: Resource limitations (funding and dedicated staff).
Small workforce and low turnover impede representation, career progression and promotion.

The self-identification form cannot measure Black and racialized gaps separately, and privacy limits disaggregation; lack of access to central systems as a separate agency; occasional resistance to changing mindsets.

organizations.notes: Goals mirror NSERC (shared human resources services). Black and racialized recruitment goals not separately set: the self-identification form cannot measure them separately. Question 4 adds that 'a structured reduction in the executive performance pay budget has also been established if goals are not met.'

commitments: Multi-year Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan with measurable baselines and targets, updated quarterly and posted on the internal website.

Employment equity made a mandatory consideration in hiring; hiring managers must review existing staffing pools first; testing name-blind evaluations and exams and interviews before screening answers.
Exploring mandatory 50% equity-deserving representation on hiring assessment boards; mapped the Employee Journey to baseline barriers.
Prioritized access to official language training for Indigenous, Black, and other racialized employees.
Indigenous Retention Initiative (February 2021): 11 advisors and 1 national manager continued under the Centre for Indigenous Statistics and Partnerships.

EDI Leadership Accountability Framework with a senior D&I leader at Director level or higher in each field; near real-time dashboards published fall 2021; Mentorship+ program for equity-deserving groups in executive and executive-feeder positions.
targets: Meet workforce availability for all equity groups by 2025 (targets set at 100%).
Self-identification rate to 100%, up from 65% in 2021.
Mandatory diversity and inclusion training for all employees by March 31, 2022.

Increase promotion rates to achieve employment equity representation at the executive level; reduce departures of EE employees for inclusion reasons; decrease drop-off rates of EE candidates in the selection process.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals aligned with WFA (2021-2025 EDI Action Plan); quarterly EE Progress Report with targets for representation, hires, and promotions based on TBS WFA.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals aligned with WFA; largest gap for visible minorities at the CR-03 level.

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goals aligned with WFA; promotion rates for EE groups compared to non-EE groups.

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals aligned with WFA; promotion rates for EE groups compared to non-EE groups.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals in the 2021-2025 EDI Action Plan: drop-off analysis in staffing processes, proportion of employees who completed mandatory awareness training, agency health via PSES and Employee Wellness Survey; exploring piloting the PCO inclusion framework.

progress: Sponsorship program: cohort 1 (August 2023, 12 matches with Director or Director General sponsors), cohort 2 (February 2024, 19 matches; Chief Statistician sponsoring 2); 31 matches total.
PE-03 recruitment process for Indigenous, Black, and racialized employees launched March 2024 (22 applicants; 0 Indigenous applicants); drop-off monitoring at all assessment milestones.
Executive Performance Management Scorecard with EE indicators, updated monthly; lack of progress affects an executive's final score and rating.
Quarterly EE Progress Report to all employees and Diversity Report to executives refreshed daily; mandatory 5-hour EDI training in all employees' performance agreements.
barriers: Official language requirements as a structural barrier for EE groups (especially Indigenous and visible minority groups) and lack of available training opportunities; CBC requirement for supervisory positions.
Lack of data for certain groups, such as 2SLGBTQIA+ and religious minorities.
Integration of 1,700 Statistical Survey Operations employees (November 2023) shifted demographics; self-identification rate fell from 87.5% to 79.4%.

organizations.notes: No targets for Black employees in the self-assessment reports since targets are based on WFA.

letter.author: Chantal Carbonneau, Registrar
commitments: Launched an internal anti-racism resources website (June 2021) and regularly share educational content on racism, reconciliation, accessibility, equity and inclusion.
Hired an experienced human resources advisor to review internal employment equity, diversity and inclusion practices, identify barriers, and review data and strategies.
Developed a 5-year employment equity, diversity and inclusion draft plan integrating the Call to Action and public service diversity and inclusion focus areas; under review and consultation.
Used targeted staffing practices (advertised and non-advertised) that reduced visible minority gaps, to be extended to other gaps.
Hold informal staffing process audits to identify current and potential barriers; monitor disaggregated survey results and operational data (promotion, mobility, tenure).

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals set in the new Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Plan, with clear goals, objectives and performance measures (special events, training and awareness campaigns, policy review); progress measured via the forthcoming Public Service Employee Survey.

progress: New Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Plan has five pillars (leadership; collaboration; policy, programs and technology; people management; reporting), each with goals, activities, timelines and performance measures reviewed every six months.
Improved representation across all employment equity groups, mostly meeting or exceeding workforce availability.
Employment Equity and Diversity Advisory Committee is active, with dedicated human resources full-time-equivalent support, consulted on policies and programs.
barriers: Small size and low turnover limit advancement opportunities for Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees.
Cannot support diverse employee networks; relies on the Employment Equity and Diversity Advisory Committee and human resources resources.
Neither the head nor the executive team has sponsored at least two Indigenous, Black or other racialized employees; no targeted recruitment campaign (advertised processes yielded few candidates).

organizations.notes: No numeric representation targets in the letter. Recruitment and promotion goals not yet set in the self-assessment (work underway).

indigenous_recruitment.text: 2022-2024 EDI Action Plan (25 commitments, four pillars): minimum 50% of new hires and 30% of new management hires from under-represented groups by 2023 (already attained); 25% of all new hires to be Indigenous persons, Black people or People of Colour at all levels, sectors and functions.

black_recruitment.text: 2022-2024 EDI Action Plan: 25% of all new hires to be Indigenous persons, Black people or People of Colour at all levels, sectors and functions.

racialized_recruitment.text: 2022-2024 EDI Action Plan: 25% of all new hires to be Indigenous persons, Black people or People of Colour at all levels, sectors and functions; minimum 50% of new hires and 30% of new management hires from under-represented groups by 2023 (already attained).

inclusion.text: 2022-2024 EDI Action Plan: support a strong sense of belonging through responsible and accountable leadership; corporate objectives and key performance indicators for EDI; gender parity and balanced representation of gender identities; enhanced self-identification to increase hiring and promotion of people living with disabilities.

progress: Hiring rate for women rose from 56% in 2020 to 81% in 2022; hiring rate for racialized groups rose from 36% to 50%.
Racialized representation rose from 23.5% in 2021 to 27% in 2022, maintaining a positive variance over market availability.
Publishes an annual employment equity report; implemented a new data collection system and self-identification questionnaire, and a Universal Accessibility Action Plan in December 2022.
Launched a reconciliation action plan in mid-October 2023 and reported intersectional results for Black Women, Women of Colour and Indigenous Women in its 2023 EDI report.
barriers: New individual-level self-identification data collection means 2022-2023 results are not directly comparable with previous fiscal years, with a disclosure threshold of three observations limiting public reporting and possible non-response bias.
Difficulty attracting and retaining Indigenous peoples as well as persons with disabilities.

organizations.notes: No promotion goals stated. Neither the head nor the executive team sponsored at least two Indigenous, Black or racialized employees; no recruitment campaign endorsed; accountability approaches not yet developed. Indigenous representation was 1.4% in 2022 (down from 1.5% in 2021), below market availability of 1.7%.

letter.author: Michael Keenan, Deputy Minister of Transport; Arun Thangaraj, Associate Deputy Minister of Transport
commitments: Launched a Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan and held a department-wide virtual town hall on diversity and inclusion (over 2,100 employees); launched Indigenous Learning Hub on National Indigenous Peoples Day.

Created a Diversity and Inclusion Secretariat with a dedicated team; two D&I Co-Champions and 10 Executive Leads for women, Indigenous peoples, Black and other racialized persons, persons with disabilities, and Positive Space/2SLGBTQIA+.

Monthly virtual coffee chats for women, Black and other racialized persons, Indigenous peoples and persons with disabilities (most recent over 800 participants); established Indigenous Employee Network and Black and other racialized persons (People of Colour) Network.
Mandatory Unconscious Bias training for all executives (in performance agreements); conversation tool for managers on racism and discrimination.
Imposed unpaid suspensions on six employees for circulating racist emails and communicated results to all employees, setting a new standard for accountability and transparency.

Will build recruitment channels and career/leadership development for Black, Indigenous, racialized and disability communities; implement a program to increase Indigenous recruitment and career development; develop an Inuit Employment Plan with Pilimmaksaivik.

Developing a performance measurement framework for the D&I Action Plan covering recruitment/retention of equity-deserving groups, self-identification and accessibility; D&I objective in every employee's performance agreement.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Multi-year recruitment and promotion goals for all EE groups using TBS workforce availability data, in the 2024-2027 Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan (expected endorsement/publication June 2024).

racialized_recruitment.text: Multi-year recruitment and promotion goals for racialized people in the 2024-2027 EDI Action Plan, using workforce availability data.

indigenous_promotion.text: Promotion goals for Indigenous employees in the 2024-2027 EDI Action Plan; talent pools of high-potential racialized/Indigenous/disability employees for executive roles and executives with ADM potential.

racialized_promotion.text: Promotion goals for racialized employees in the 2024-2027 EDI Action Plan; same talent pools.

inclusion.text: Inclusion goals under development in the 2024-2027 EDI Action Plan, including PSES targets on EDI questions; Indigenous Career Navigator program (40+ presentations, 80+ consultations, 25+ external Indigenous applicants guided); Centre of Expertise for Accommodations (2024-25); Black and Other Racialized Employee Network informal mentorship program.

progress: Indigenous Career Navigator delivered 40+ presentations, 80+ consultation sessions, guided 25+ external Indigenous applicants and spoke with 192+ hiring managers.
Four advertised processes targeted EE groups with over 100 EE candidates qualifying; results shared with other departments.

Leadership Development Initiative third cohort launched fall 2023 with 70% EE group participants; Mentorship Plus pilot in Safety and Security Group (April 2023-March 2024); two employees selected for TBS Mosaic program.
Performance Measurement Framework for the 2024-2027 EDI Action Plan due early fall 2024; monthly people management dashboards and Annual Workforce Analysis Scorecards track representation.
barriers: Many positions require specialized skills (e.g., inspectors), shrinking the candidate pool and the EE candidate pool further.

Amended Official Languages Act Part V (CBC/CBC for management) may make it harder to appoint Indigenous, Black, racialized people and persons with disabilities to executive and supervisory roles in bilingual regions.
Setting quantitative inclusion goals is hard due to lack of comparative data; exit survey data not usable due to low response rate.

commitments: Update the three-year departmental Employment Equity Plan with quantitative and qualitative goals and a monitoring process; reignite the Diversity Committee.
Review statements of merit criteria, staffing assessment tools and processes over three years to ensure they are inclusive and do not create systemic barriers.
Create a continuous anticipatory staffing inventory targeting designated groups for specific positions; monitor use of staffing flexibilities, designated-group participation and drop-off rates.
Provide Positive Space training to Executive and Diversity Committee members and Indigenous Relations training to employees; run Safe Space sessions.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Objective in the 2023-2026 Employment Equity Plan to increase employees recruited and/or promoted within underrepresented designated groups to achieve a representative workforce, based on annual gap analysis from Treasury Board Secretariat Workforce Analysis Reports.

progress: Launched several continuous anticipatory staffing inventories targeting designated groups for technical positions, personally endorsed by the Deputy Head.
In 2023, at least one Indigenous, Black or racialized employee was hired non-imperatively; official language training prioritized for those who require it.
Semi-annual employment equity data shared with senior management and the Diversity Committee; annual gap analysis updated and documented in the Employment Equity Plan shared with all employees.
Executives have the overarching commitment 'Advancing Anti-Racism, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in the Public Service' in performance management agreements.
barriers: Small, highly specialized workforce (about 220 employees): recruitment from a small labour pool (air, rail sectors) where designated groups are underrepresented; departures (retirement, competitive labour market) erode gains in closing gaps.
Workforce availability data often suppressed due to small size, making monitoring, reporting and follow-up hard; delayed modernization of centralized self-declaration tools.

Technical staff show limited interest in managerial/EX roles (satisfaction as technical experts; management roles often pay less); the Treasury Board Direction on prescribed presence in the workplace limited flexible working arrangements that aided recruitment.

organizations.notes: No inclusion goals set in the 2024 self-assessment (organization has not yet set these goals); it relies on Public Service Employee Survey diversity and inclusion results.

letter.author: Peter Wallace, Secretary; Erin O'Gorman, Associate Secretary; Christine Donoghue, Chief Human Resources Officer; Roch Huppé, Comptroller General; Catherine Luelo, Chief Information Officer; Yazmine Laroche, Deputy Minister, Public Service Accessibility
commitments: Released eight sets of disaggregated enterprise data covering 21 employment equity subgroups (including Black, Métis and Inuit employees) and launched an online interactive data visualization tool (April 2021).
Launched the Self-Identification Modernization Project (September 2020), with a new co-designed questionnaire to be implemented in fall 2021.

Modified the Executive Leadership Development Program (September 2020) so at least 50% of EX-01 to EX-03 nominees are from persons with disabilities, Indigenous peoples or visible minority groups, and launched the Mentorship Plus program (December 2020), with 36 departments implementing it.
Wrote to all deputy heads detailing how many employees with disabilities each must hire to close representation gaps, supporting the commitment to hire 5,000 persons with disabilities by 2025.

Created a Designated Senior Official for Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion community of practice (91% of departments have identified one) and the Federal Speakers' Forum for Diversity and Inclusion (38 speakers).

Internally, journey-mapped Black employees' experiences with the Black Employees Network, required every staffing action to explain how diversity and inclusion were considered, and added anti-racism and accessibility commitments to every executive's performance agreement.
targets: Hire 5,000 persons with disabilities by 2025 (public-service-wide commitment).
At least 50% of Executive Leadership Development Program nominees (EX-01 to EX-03) from persons with disabilities, Indigenous peoples or visible minority groups.

progress: The Mentorship Plus third cohort graduated 23 participants in 2023-24; both Mosaic Leadership Development participants (2022-23 and 2023-24) received and accepted EX-01 offers.

The Secretary endorsed an EX-03 recruitment process focused on Indigenous, Black and racialized employees in 2023-24, yielding seven qualified candidates; a special employment equity recruitment team was endorsed by all deputy ministers.
Allocated $300,000 in 2023-24 and 2024-25 to support equity-seeking employee networks (Indigenous, Black, Accessibility, 2SLGBTQIA+, Women's).

The workforce intelligence dashboard gives all employees access to employment equity data; in 2023-24 visible minority representation (524) exceeded the workforce availability goal (488), while Indigenous representation (54) remained 10 below its goal (64).
barriers: Resource constraints: financial (budget restrictions, competing priorities), human resources (recruiting, training and retaining qualified staff) and technological infrastructure.
Organizational resistance to change, including ingrained practices, bureaucratic inertia, legacy systems and established norms, plus cultural resistance and individual attitudes.
Current data does not allow identifying gaps within specific occupational groups and does not include recruitment and promotion goals.

organizations.notes: Recruitment, promotion and inclusion goals are all 'work underway' rather than set; TBS is exploring workforce availability combined with a 5% turnover rate plus an additional 5% to set targets. Internal data annex: women +5.4%, Indigenous +9.8%, visible minorities +9.8%, persons with disabilities +10.3% in 2020-21, with remaining gaps for Indigenous peoples (5 below target) and persons with disabilities (63 below target); a gap of six Indigenous executives.

letter.author: Paul Ledwell, Deputy Minister
commitments: More focused action plan (October 2020) on culture change, workforce diversity and representation, and positive employment policies and practices.
National recruitment initiative welcoming hundreds of new employees to the Service Delivery Branch; two new executives from EE communities.
Renewed National Diversity and Inclusion Advisory Committee (15 diverse employees and 3 bargaining agents); new equity, diversity, and anti-racism taskforce.
Accessibility Network gap analysis for the seven priority areas in the Accessible Canada Act.
Common D&I performance commitment in all executives' performance agreements.

Complete an Employment Systems Review; multi-year staffing strategy; targeted selection processes for EX-1 feeder groups; implement Mentorship Plus (sponsorship component); measurement framework tracking progress quarterly; new multi-year D&I action plan.

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment targets set in the 2023-2025 Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan 'We All Belong' for Executive and non-Executive employees, based on departmental WFA; monitored quarterly; each ADM created a Branch-level plan with goals per equity group.

black_recruitment.text: Recruitment targets set in the 2023-2025 Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan 'We All Belong' for Executive and non-Executive employees, based on departmental WFA; monitored quarterly.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment targets set in the 2023-2025 Diversity and Inclusion Action Plan 'We All Belong' for Executive and non-Executive employees, based on departmental WFA; targets for sub-groups of visible minorities using own representation data.

inclusion.text: Minimum inclusion criteria based on PSES key questions in four areas (Career Development and Accommodation, Inclusive Workplace, Harassment and Discrimination, Anti-Racism); goal is to increase each equity group's percentage versus non-equity groups; baselines from 2020 PSES adjusted against 2022 results.

progress: Mentorship Plus first sponsorship cohort: senior leaders sponsored 6 EE group members (2 Indigenous, 2 racialized); second cohort being matched.

DM-endorsed EE process for EX-minus-one level for Indigenous, persons with disabilities, and racialized employees; first consideration required before any other staffing option; over a dozen other departments granted access to the pool.

Diversity and Inclusion Governance Model established 2023: Executive Inclusion Officer (new position), Champion of Inclusion, designated champions, Champion Council, and Equity Community Advisory Committee.
Culture impacts between 2020 and 2022 PSES: harassment reports fell 10% to 9% (visible minorities) and 14% to 7% (Indigenous); employees feeling valued 71% to 73% (visible minorities 69% to 77%).
After anti-racism training reaching over 1,000 employees, knowledge of how to recognize racism rose 43% and allyship skills increased 66%.
barriers: Limited access to disaggregated workforce availability data and delay in launching the new self-identification process.
Inability to receive PSES data by equity community and Branch.
Homogeneous population at Head Office in Charlottetown and availability of candidates; lack of information about communities under the visible minority umbrella.

organizations.notes: Letter data annex is August 2021; annex notes WFA is used as a floor or minimum reference, not a ceiling. No promotion goals selected in the self-assessment.

letter.author: Christopher J. McNeil, Chair
commitments: Initiated a Diversity and Inclusion Committee of Members and staff to consider diversity and inclusion issues and recommend to senior management.
Developed a Vision for a Healthy, Inclusive and Diverse VRAB (2020) and added diversity and inclusion to the Board's statement of Values (2021).

Contribute with Veterans Affairs human resources to an Employment Equity Strategy covering recruitment, promotion, sponsorship, development and retention of Black and other racialized people, Indigenous people, persons with disabilities and equity-seeking employees.

Members participated in the KAIROS Blanket exercise and other diversity and inclusion training; staff encouraged to take Canada School of Public Service diversity and inclusion and harassment prevention training.
Develop an Accessibility Action Plan with Veterans Affairs Canada; develop a more diverse and inclusive approach to administering the oath at hearings.
Work with Veterans Affairs human resources on potential mandatory training for managers on unconscious bias and anti-racism, and for onboarding new employees.

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals set using current employee representation data, workforce availability data and the resultant gap.

Onboarding requires all employees to complete four mandatory Canada School of Public Service courses (Gender-Based Analysis Plus, Adopting an Inclusive Mindset, Reflecting on Cultural Bias: Indigenous Perspectives, and the Rex Murphy racism response).
Supports hiring managers with diverse, accessible and inclusive staffing tools, including Public Service Commission pools for persons with disabilities and other equity groups.
Official language training priority is given to Indigenous, Black and other racialized staff after need, area and baseline level.
barriers: Small size means representation rates are often not disclosed because they could identify employees.

The head has not personally endorsed a recruitment campaign for Indigenous, Black or other racialized employees.

letter.author: Guylaine Roy, Deputy Minister of Women and Gender Equality
commitments: Implemented mandatory anti-racism and anti-oppression training completed by all employees, plus mandatory unconscious bias training and coaching for all executives including Intercultural Development Inventory assessments.

Put hiring manager commitments in performance agreements to support recruitment and retention of Black, racialized and Indigenous employees and employees with disabilities, using targeted programs (Federal Internship for Newcomers, Indigenous Student Employment, Visible Minority Student Program).
Conducted a Gender-based Analysis Plus of all hiring policies, tools and practices, leading to modified job ads, interviews, representative selection boards and a Hiring Guide for managers.
Implemented a mentorship program through the Young Professionals Network and an official languages training strategy in fall 2020 (69 employees benefited).
Developed a Reconciliation Framework with the Indigenous Advisory Network and made Gender-based Analysis Plus training mandatory for all employees.
Built two gender-inclusive washrooms, installed touchless doors, and provided guidance and software for accessible documents.
targets: New staffing plan to set targets at minimum workforce availability for each employment equity group (planned).

indigenous_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals focused on surpassing workforce availability; as of March 31, 2024, Indigenous representation was 3.9% versus 3.6% workforce availability (goal met).

racialized_recruitment.text: Recruitment goals focused on surpassing workforce availability; as of March 31, 2024, racialized representation was 22.8% versus 18.0% workforce availability (goal met).

inclusion.text: Renewing the Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Accessibility Strategy and Action Plan (IDEASAP) and Indigenous Recruitment, Retention, and Advancement Strategy and Action Plan (IRRASAP) for 2024-2027; three of four 2023-24 Corporate Commitments focused on wellness, inclusion, diversity, equity and accessibility, and anti-racism; minimum four hours of IDEA and anti-racism training in all performance agreements.

progress: As of March 31, 2024, representation exceeds workforce availability across all employment equity groups: women 85.3% vs 64.5%, racialized 22.8% vs 18.0%, persons with disabilities 9.4% vs 9.1%, Indigenous 3.9% vs 3.6%.
Established a Workforce Management Committee in August 2023 with an equity lens on hiring, promotion and development for equity-seeking groups.

Two EC-04/EC-05 recruitment processes qualified 21 individuals from racialized groups and 5 individuals with disabilities; all selection committee members undergo mandatory inclusive recruitment training.
Implemented an Inclusion Stewards program to identify and mitigate biases in performance management, starting with executives.
barriers: Small department of about 450 full-time equivalents with limited human and financial resources; network work is done on top of regular duties and consultations take longer.
Limited human resources data capacity and maturity for measuring progress, including extracting, preparing, analyzing and disseminating quality data in a timely manner.

Budget reductions ended temporary employment, raising questions about the impact on Indigenous, Black and other racialized employees in temporary positions; no disaggregated data available for Black employees.

organizations.notes: No separate Black goals and no disaggregated data for Black employees; no formal promotion goals due to small size and infrequent opportunities. EX-01 pool established in 2022 prioritizes employment equity group candidates.
